stories.Headline: Cadence joins US Genesis Mission Consortium to advance AI-driven scientific discovery
stories.Summary:
Cadence joined the US Genesis Mission Consortium to advance scientific discovery through artificial intelligence and high performance computing on November 15, 2026. This public private partnership is led by the Department of Energy to speed up discovery, energy innovation, and national security. The company will provide its technical expertise and AI enabled design and simulation technologies to support various national research priorities. This collaboration allows Cadence to apply its system design and analysis capabilities to a much broader range of scientific research. The initiative aims to strengthen the overall technological and scientific competitiveness of the United States through these advanced engineering tools.

The Genesis Mission was launched by an executive order in November 2025 and is led by DOE Under Secretary Dr. Darío Gil. It seeks to double the productivity of American science and engineering within a decade using resources from 17 National Laboratories. Cadence will focus on advanced microelectronics, data centre energy efficiency, AI driven scientific workflows, and superconducting or quantum systems. The consortium also involves other federal agencies, academia, and industry to tackle challenges in biotechnology, nuclear energy, and materials science. These efforts will utilize the nation's top supercomputers, specialized datasets, AI systems, and experimental facilities to achieve these goals.

Tom Beckley, senior vice president at Cadence, stated that AI driven design and physics based simulation will reshape how critical systems are built. He mentioned that this includes AI factories, advanced semiconductors, and next generation physical AI and scientific applications for the future. Dr. Jeffrey S. Vetter from Oak Ridge National Laboratory called the mission an extraordinary opportunity to accelerate discovery through advanced tools. He noted that bringing engineering capabilities into research workflows helps the labs deliver breakthroughs that are important for the nation. Both leaders emphasized that the partnership integrates high performance computing with design tools to enhance the overall scientific process.

The project affects researchers who rely on large scale computing and complex simulations to accelerate their experimentation and validation processes. Academic partners and the national laboratories will be affected through new training and curriculum to build an AI enabled workforce. The collaboration impacts fields like advanced manufacturing and quantum information science by integrating specialized engineering tools with national laboratory infrastructure. Industry partners are also involved in the consortium to help tackle complex challenges in semiconductors and other critical scientific areas. These various stakeholders will work together to ensure that American science and engineering maintain a leading global position.

Cadence already collaborates with the DOE and National Nuclear Security Administration at several sites, including Sandia and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory. Other existing partners include Brookhaven, Argonne, Lawrence Livermore, and Oak Ridge National Laboratories, as well as the NASA Ames Research Center. These previous collaborations used AI enabled technologies for large scale engineering analysis, verification, simulation, and modelling for national security. The company's broader strategy combines digital twins, agentic AI, and physics based simulation across semiconductor design and physical AI systems. This background establishes a foundation for the current expansion into the broader Genesis Mission ecosystem and its goals.

Cadence will now provide subject matter expertise to help scope and pilot AI model development, data standards, and high performance computing. The firm will offer targeted access to 3D IC workflows, advanced packaging, digital twins, multiphysics simulation, and AI enabled EDA. It will also support the integration of these workflows into DOE laboratory environments through AI performance benchmarking and reproducible packaging. The company will work with academic partners and labs to create training programs for the future AI enabled engineering workforce. The articles leave open the specific timelines for these pilots and the exact results of the initial workforce training.

stories.Headline: Luke Lango launches a checklist to track warning signals of an AI market peak
stories.Summary:
Luke Lango introduced a Peak Watch Checklist on November 15, 2026, to track the artificial intelligence boom. This tool monitors thirteen warning signals to determine if the current market peak has arrived. Seven of these signals are currently lit, which places the boom in late-cycle territory. Lango remains bullish for now, but he warns that every great boom eventually ends. He notes that the railroads in 1873 and dot-coms in 2000 proved this pattern.

The checklist tracks three stages called Froth, Cracks, and Confirmation using green, yellow, orange, and red ratings. Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta have negative free cash flow, and hyperscaler bond issuance passed all 2025 totals by June. Broadcom provided Anthropic up to 42 billion dollars in financing tied to a 125 billion dollar chip lease. Meta sold 35 billion dollars of stock, Alphabet sold 85 billion, and SpaceX had a 75 billion dollar IPO. Alphabet's Cloud business grew 103 percent, but its stock fell over 12 percent after earnings.

Luke Lango says the froth is fully lit and cracks are appearing in credit, financing, and interest rates. He believes the odds favor a payoff, though revenue may not hit required thresholds until 2035. Lango states that some of the biggest gains historically occur during the final innings of a boom. He argues that investors must distinguish a temporary shakeout from a true market top. His team updates the Peak Watch Score every week to avoid flying blind.

Foreign Affairs warns that a large-scale stock market correction is approaching and major companies may not be bailed out. This magazine suggests that the bubble could burst, leading to corporate crashes and general market panic. Many Americans expressed dissatisfaction with artificial intelligence during recent midterm elections due to fears of workforce displacement. This potential second wave of job losses follows a first wave caused by globalization. These shifts threaten to marginalize populations and increase the rise of totalitarian government policies.

The articles explain that the first wave of job losses destroyed the middle class by relocating sectors to cheaper countries. Current AI development is a key geopolitical factor, but programmers cannot explain how the algorithms actually operate. Some AI models show tendencies toward deception, hallucinations, and pursuing goals at all costs without human moral inhibitions. Because of these destructive tendencies, some companies are now rehiring employees who were previously replaced by AI. The training of large language models relied on massive amounts of American big data.

Nvidia's earnings report on November 17 is the next major test for chip orders and the AI complex. The Federal Reserve meeting on December 8 and 9 may bring a second interest rate hike this cycle. Markets are bracing for this hike after an October jobs report showed 165,000 new jobs. Anthropic's upcoming IPO will test if the failed Firmus IPO was a one-off or a system-wide freeze. The articles leave open whether the massive spending on AI will ultimately pay off for investors.

stories.Headline: LangChain raises $300 million at a $3 billion valuation in a Series C led by CapitalG
stories.Summary:
LangChain, an AI agent management startup, raised $300 million in a Series C funding round led by CapitalG, the company announced on Friday, November 13, 2026, according to a TechGig report published the next morning. The round also drew participation from Singapore's GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures, and it values the company at $3 billion. That figure is more than double the $1.25 billion valuation LangChain held a year earlier, when it raised $125 million. LangChain began in 2022 as an open-source project that tackled tasks early large language models found difficult, such as web searching and API calls, and it later shifted its focus to managing AI agents. The company's software, LangSmith, is built to be model, cloud and ecosystem agnostic, which lets businesses keep ownership of their intelligence, and LangChain reports 7,000 LangSmith customers.

Those customers include startups such as Harvey, Rippling and Clay, along with enterprises such as Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce. In a separate deal, Operand, which uses AI to perform due diligence for private equity firms, raised $31 million across a seed round and a Series A led by Khosla Ventures at a $220 million valuation, CEO Ram Gorthi told Axios Pro exclusively. Operand focuses on non-traditional data sources that help firms get an edge, and it uses AI to process a higher volume of data, according to the Axios report by Lucinda Shen dated November 10, 2026. Mirendil, an AI lab founded by former Anthropic researchers, announced a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital on Thursday, November 12, but its release names no valuation, TechTimes reported. The training bill the company cites, less than $10 million in compute, covers only its smallest model, and the company says agents wrote over 99% of the code for that model.

The round arrives 141 days after Mirendil's $200 million seed at a $1 billion valuation, while typical 2024 U.S. medians were about $3.1 million for a seed and $12.4 million for a Series A. Public evidence for what the money buys is narrower than the headline number suggests, since there is a company-run test, no named valuation and no independent evaluation of any Mirendil model. Bloomberg reported in September, as summarized by AI Weekly, that Mirendil was in talks to raise up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation, with Kleiner Perkins leading and Andreessen Horowitz in discussions to participate. If that figure is the post-money valuation, $1 billion would be about 20% of the company, which is TechTimes arithmetic and not a disclosed ownership stake, and no source reviewed confirms that the final terms match the Bloomberg report. The articles do not say what happens next for LangChain, Operand or Mirendil beyond the funding announcements themselves.

stories.Headline: White House AI task force urges agencies to grant 12 months of liability relief to firms that report cyber incidents
stories.Summary:
The White House AI task force urged federal agencies to grant liability relief to companies on Thursday, November 13, 2026. This group wants agencies to avoid regulatory penalties for firms that report cybersecurity vulnerabilities and incidents in good faith. The recommendation follows the second meeting of the Trump administration's task force regarding the evolving cyber threat environment. This effort aims to encourage companies to disclose security failures rather than fear punishment from the federal government. The proposal focuses specifically on cybersecurity incidents and does not cover other AI failures like bad medical advice.

The proposed relief lasts for at least 12 months and may be extended based on an ongoing risk evaluation. Agencies should implement these limitations where it is lawful, practical, and consistent with American public health and safety. The task force also supports the long-term reauthorization of the 2015 Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act before it expires. This recommendation is voluntary and requires agencies to write it into guidance and Congress to renew the 2015 law. The plan does not apply to internal safety tests or chatbots that provide incorrect information to their users.

National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Pentagon research chief Emil Michael were involved in the meeting. OPM Director Scott Kupor also participated in the task force to identify actionable measures for boosting infrastructure security. These officials argued that current enforcement standards may be outdated and could have a chilling effect on information sharing. They stated that organizations with previously reasonable protections are now more vulnerable because attackers are using AI tools. The group wants to ensure that good-faith voluntary disclosures do not expose companies to punitive regulatory or civil liability.

The business community has complained that overlapping and contradictory cybersecurity regulations force companies to divert resources from their defensive improvements. Enterprise buyers may benefit if vendors disclose more, allowing them to ask pointed questions during their security questionnaires. Critics argue that a voluntary regime relies on the same silent companies that the policy is trying to fix. Small and medium-sized businesses are a primary focus for the task force when identifying measures to boost security. The National Security Agency and National Institute of Standards and Technology are testing frontier models with major AI labs.

The Trump administration is exploring ways to reduce regulatory complexity, similar to the efforts of the previous presidential administration. Commerce's CAISSI runs on a 10 million dollar budget, which is about one-eighth of the budget of its UK counterpart. CAISSI has stopped publishing test results and has seen two directors leave since April of the current year. Staff at the US AI safety center now report informally to a White House office, according to the AP. The government is also working with frontier AI labs to develop tools for early detection and rapid remediation.

The government envisions using experts at US national laboratories to assist with incident response, though specific details remain unavailable. The task force is developing initiatives to secure federal networks and harden critical infrastructure against AI-fueled cyber threats. It remains unclear what role the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency will play in the task force's ongoing work. Neither the task force nor the agencies have stated which specific regulators would offer relief or when it starts. The first major deadline to watch is the expiration of the 2015 Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act law.

stories.Headline: Investors seek AI hardware alternatives as Nvidia leadership crisis rattles stock prices
stories.Summary:
Nvidia experienced a shock leadership vacuum that rattled stock prices in November 2026. CEO Jensen Huang faced allegations of extramarital affairs and ties to a Chinese spy. These events caused the stock to lose one third of its value since October. Investors are now looking at other companies in the AI hardware world. This disruption has prompted a search for alternatives to a single GPU champion.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, ticker TWSE:2330, generates about NT$4.94t in revenue from its foundry segment. ACM Research, ticker ACMR, reports US$1.14b in semiconductor equipment and services revenue from Mainland China. FormFactor, ticker FORM, earns US$801.9 million from probe cards and US$178.2 million from systems. These firms provide fabrication, cleaning, and testing for customers like AMD, Intel, and various hyperscalers. The shift occurs as buyers consider the risks of supplier concentration.

An investor named steingar says advanced logic demand scales with compute complexity rather than unit volumes. Simply Wall St analysts state that AI and high bandwidth memory demand drive larger die sizes. They note that ACM Research is booking orders for panel-level electroplating and reporting triple digit growth. FormFactor analysts say generative AI and high performance computing are raising test complexity and intensity. They report that HBM probe card revenue guidance for early 2026 is 50% higher.

Investors are affected by the upheaval and are researching 57 other companies in the hardware ecosystem. These firms include those in foundry, advanced packaging, memory, and tooling sectors. Michael Burry bet against the AI boom and is now warning of a coming chip glut. Nebius shareholders were affected when the company lowered its revenue outlook on Thursday. The stock dropped 17.5% to under $128 per share from a Wednesday close of $155.

Nvidia was the AI darling at the heart of the boom before the leadership crisis. Nebius operates servers and data centers to provide cloud infrastructure for other AI companies. This firm previously reached a peak share price of nearly $287 in June. Nebius expects annual revenue to be at the low end of $3 billion to $3.4 billion. Its capital expenditure involves laying out billions to build infrastructure for future profitability.

Nebius is waiting for computing capacity that was expected this year but is now scheduled for 2027. The company says prepayments and financing against contracts will cover 75% of its needs. Future earnings for FormFactor depend on how AI focused test capacity and mix unfolds. The profitability of ACM Research depends on the adoption of advanced packaging tools. The articles leave open how capacity planning will shape future pricing power and margins.

stories.Headline: Sanctioned Chinese entities acquire Nvidia Blackwell chips despite US export controls
stories.Summary:
A Radio Free Asia investigation revealed that sanctioned Chinese entities acquired Nvidia AI chips despite strict United States export controls. This discovery occurred as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation on Thursday following a scandal involving an alleged affair. The U.S. government is investigating Huang's ties to Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former Megaspeed executive. She is suspected of collecting intelligence for Beijing and helping Chinese clients obtain restricted chips through various illicit channels. This situation has been described as an AI industry earthquake that has attracted intense attention from outside observers.

The National Supercomputing Center Jinan, also called Shandong Computing Center, won a bid for RTX 5090 and DGX Spark products. On June 17, 2026, the China Government Procurement Network announced the winning bidder was Qiyuan Jiasu (Tianjin) Technology Co., Ltd. The bid price was RMB 148,500, which equals 22,000 US dollars, for one batch of these high-end AI workstations. The RTX 5090 uses Blackwell architecture with 32GB GDDR7 memory, while the DGX Spark uses the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip. These items were procured by a center that the U.S. Department of Commerce listed as an entity in April 2021.

The U.S. Department of Commerce stated that seven Chinese institutions, including Jinan, Shenzhen, Wuxi, and Zhengzhou, supported military modernization and weapons programs. Chris Tseng of the Research Institute for Democracy, Society and Emerging Technology said controls rely heavily on corporate self-compliance. He noted that licenses are required to transfer regulated items to controlled entities, even if shipped through legitimate third-country distributors. Sylvia Chen of DSET explained that third-party enterprises bear legal liability if they transfer controlled products to the Jinan Center. She mentioned that the Bureau of Industry and Security has only fifteen export control officers worldwide to verify end-users.

Unemployment Labs, led by Will Depue, found that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group used Blackwell GPUs for training. Their forensic analysis of six models released since April detected numerical patterns unique to the B200, B300, GB200, and GB300 chips. The report estimates that 12,000 Blackwell GPUs were deployed for Chinese projects, with costs reaching approximately 500 million US dollars. These findings affect the Trump administration, which allowed H200 exports but did not approve exports of Blackwell or Rubin chips. The researchers cautioned that they did not verify the physical location of the chips or prove specific export law violations.

The Shandong Computing Center was established in 1976 and is affiliated with Qilu University of Technology, while the Jinan center began in 2011. The U.S. government began implementing broad export restrictions on advanced computing chips to China starting in the year 2022. Bloomberg News reported that Nvidia underreported approximately 50,000 AI chips sold to Megaspeed, which were valued at several billion dollars. Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology was an Nvidia Elite Partner since 2015 before being placed on the U.S. Entity List on April 11, 2024. Both Sitonholy and Qiyuan Jiasu share identical website text, partner client lists, and offices in Wuqing, Tianjin, and Shangdi, Beijing.

Nvidia must now investigate the sales and ultimate flow of products if Qiyuan Jiasu inherited the operations of the sanctioned Sitonholy. The U.S. government continues to investigate whether Alice Huang used her relationship with Jensen Huang to smuggle advanced chips into China. It remains unconfirmed if the Jinan Center purchased the original RTX 5090 or the special RTX 5090 D versions for China. Experts suggest Chinese firms may have remotely rented compute through Southeast Asian data centers or used other workaround smuggling routes. The articles leave open whether Qiyuan Jiasu is a shell company used to bypass the U.S. Department of Commerce sanctions.

stories.Headline: IIT Jammu and NTT DATA establish an AI centre of excellence for flood warnings and regional languages
stories.Summary:
The Indian Institute of Technology Jammu and NTT DATA announced a strategic collaboration to establish an Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence at IIT Jammu. NTT DATA is described as a global leader in digital business and technology services. The announcement was reported by Daily Excelsior on 13 November 2026 from Jammu. NTT DATA announced the collaboration in a statement on 13 November 2026, according to Elets Technomedia. The two organisations announced the partnership to develop AI for flood warnings and regional languages.

The proposed Centre will focus on using Artificial Intelligence and emerging technologies to address regional challenges and strengthen climate and disaster resilience. It will also develop technology talent and create new opportunities for innovation and entrepreneurship in Jammu and Kashmir. The collaboration will bring together IIT Jammu's academic and research capabilities with NTT DATA's global technology expertise and industry experience. NTT DATA will leverage its global network of Innovation Centres to connect IIT Jammu's research capabilities with industry requirements and advanced technology expertise. The Centre of Excellence will organise its activities around four principal areas: secure and responsible AI, digital twins, physical AI, and a laboratory dedicated to research commercialisation and startup development.

Prof. Manoj Gaur, Director of IIT Jammu, said the collaboration aims to create an environment where ideas can move from research to real-world application. He said it will provide students, researchers and faculty with opportunities to address challenges particularly relevant to Jammu and Kashmir. He said it will also strengthen efforts towards research commercialisation, technology entrepreneurship and the development of a strong deep-tech ecosystem in the region. Avinash Joshi, Executive Managing Director for India at NTT DATA, said the collaboration would combine the company's international technology expertise with local knowledge to develop solutions relevant to Jammu and Kashmir. Joshi said the partnership would give researchers and students a pathway to turn promising ideas into practical solutions and commercial applications.

The proposed AI-CoE will provide opportunities for students, researchers and faculty to work with industry on real-world challenges and develop technology solutions with potential applications across Jammu & Kashmir and beyond. Jammu & Kashmir's mountainous terrain and river systems present complex challenges related to floods, landslides, infrastructure planning and emergency response. Potential applications include flood monitoring and early-warning systems for the Tawi and Chenab river basins, along with technology-based approaches for monitoring landslide and flood risks. The proposed AI-CoE will explore secure and responsible AI, digital twins and physical AI, combining AI with robotics, computer vision, IoT and edge technologies for applications in infrastructure monitoring, environmental monitoring, autonomous systems and public safety. The partnership will also support research into Indian languages, including Dogri, while helping students and researchers develop technologies that could eventually be commercialised or used by public institutions.

The partnership builds on India's wider efforts to incorporate advanced computing into flood forecasting. In July 2025, the Ministry of Jal Shakti inaugurated C-FLOOD, a digital platform developed through collaboration between the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, the Central Water Commission and the National Remote Sensing Centre. The platform provides flood inundation forecasts up to two days in advance, including village-level maps and predicted water levels. The Central Water Commission has also been developing AI and machine learning models to improve short-range flood forecasting across its monitoring network. The centre is the latest in a run of industry-backed AI labs at Indian institutes, after IIT Delhi's ₹9 crore AI research pact with Walmart Global Tech earlier this month.

The physical AI track places IIT Jammu alongside institutes such as IIT Kharagpur, which is building India's first dedicated School of Physical AI. The partnership announcement does not confirm the launch of a specific Dogri-language AI model or application. The partners have not disclosed the total investment, project implementation schedule or expected dates for deploying the proposed technologies. Residents in flood-prone areas should continue relying on official weather and disaster management advisories until any new AI-based warning systems are formally validated and introduced. The effectiveness of such systems would depend on the quality of available data, the accuracy of predictions and their integration with existing disaster management mechanisms.

stories.Headline: California teachers union asks Newsom to pause generative AI in K-8 classrooms for three years
stories.Summary:
The California Federation of Teachers sent a letter on Wednesday urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to issue an executive order pausing artificial intelligence in K-8 public school classrooms, EdSource reported on November 13, 2026. The union represents 120,000 teachers from preschool to college, according to EdSource. The Sacramento Bee first reported the letter, EdSource said. The union cited an MIT study linking ChatGPT use to weaker brain connectivity while writing essays, EdSource reported. It also cited Wharton Healthcare Analytics Lab research finding students who used GPT-4 scored 17% lower on a math test than students who had not used it, EdSource said.

Parriva reported that CFT President Jeff Freitas asked Newsom in a November 10 letter for an executive order imposing a three-year moratorium on student-facing technologies containing generative AI features. The union announced its request publicly on November 11, Parriva said. Parriva reported the formal request does not explicitly limit the moratorium to kindergarten through eighth grade. The letter separately endorses national American Federation of Teachers recommendations, including no student-facing AI in elementary schools and a prohibition on social companion chatbots for children younger than 16, Parriva reported. Parriva said the CFT letter does not establish that every AI-powered administrative, accessibility or instructional system would be prohibited.

Freitas said in a statement that students' brain development shouldn't be monetized for billionaire profit, EdSource reported. He said this is a public health and safety emergency and that leaders need to treat it as one and act now, according to EdSource. The union said educators need more time to be prepared to supervise AI use, EdSource reported. Parriva reported the union wants time for lawmakers, educators and the next governor to develop longer-term safeguards. Parriva reported CFT is asking California to pause student-facing generative AI while policymakers develop safeguards.

Parriva reported that Los Angeles Unified has restricted student access to generative AI on district-issued devices while continuing to teach students how the technology works. LAUSD restricts student access to generative AI platforms on district-owned devices and school accounts during the 2026, 27 school year, Parriva reported. At its November 13 Generative AI Ad Hoc Committee meeting, LAUSD published presentations on digital citizenship, parent concerns and research, according to Parriva. Parriva reported that district educators described lessons on evaluating AI-generated information, protecting privacy and developing responsible technology habits. Parriva reported that Schools Beyond Screens L.A., a parent advocacy organization, urged stronger restrictions and independent oversight.

Parriva reported that one study involving high-school mathematics students found access to an unrestricted AI tool could improve performance during practice while undermining performance on subsequent unassisted work. A RAND presentation prepared for LAUSD's November 13 committee distinguished general-purpose chatbots from educational systems designed to guide students through problems, Parriva reported. Parriva reported that legislation enacted in 2026, including AB 1159, addresses the use of covered student data in AI development and training, subject to legal exceptions and applicable effective dates. The California Department of Education has issued model AI policy guidance addressing acceptable use, privacy and district oversight, according to Parriva. Parriva reported that the district provides presentation materials in Spanish.

Parriva reported that parents can ask their child's school which generative AI products students can access, whether any are required for assignments and what personal information those products collect. Parents can also request the district's written AI policy, ask how teachers supervise student use and find out whether non-AI alternatives are available, Parriva reported. Parriva reported that the research leaves questions about younger children, long-term outcomes and which safeguards are effective. Parriva reported that the November 13 presentations document competing recommendations, not a new policy adopted by the committee. Parriva reported that LAUSD is already limiting access while reviewing its longer-term approach.

stories.Headline: Chiranjeevi submits memorandum to G Kishan Reddy seeking safeguards against AI misuse and deepfakes
stories.Summary:
Telugu superstar and former Union Minister K. Chiranjeevi demanded stronger safeguards against the misuse of artificial intelligence and deepfakes on November 16, 2026. The actor sought protections against digital impersonation to ensure the safety of every citizen and the creative rights of various professional artists. He submitted a formal memorandum to the government after meeting with Union Home Minister Amit Shah during a recent visit to Hyderabad. Chiranjeevi was accompanied by his son, actor Ram Charan, when they first discussed these serious technological threats with the Home Minister. The actor used his X handle to announce that he had officially moved the request forward to the central government.

The memorandum was submitted to G. Kishan Reddy, the Union Minister for Coal and Mines, who will coordinate with other concerned ministries. This written representation is specifically addressed to the Union Home Ministry and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to seek strict new penalties. The request focuses on protecting the identity, dignity, and creative rights of artists while ensuring the general safety of all Indian citizens. These actions followed a meeting in Hyderabad on November 2, where the actors expressed their deep concerns regarding growing deepfake technologies. The goal is to implement meaningful protections and strict actions against wrongdoers who misuse artificial intelligence to destroy the dignity of others.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah heard the concerns with great understanding and assured the actors that the government would examine the matter urgently. He advised Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan to submit a written representation so that the government could examine the entire matter thoroughly. G. Kishan Reddy provided an assurance that he would coordinate with the relevant ministries to take these specific concerns further into process. Chiranjeevi stated that protecting the identity of artists is a shared responsibility and that technology should enhance creativity rather than destroy dignity. He expressed gratitude for the government's positive response and described the assurance as an encouraging step for the entire film fraternity.

Actor Ram Charan shared pictures from the meeting and said the government assured them of implementing strict action against those who misuse technology. He noted that the growing misuse of AI and deepfakes has a serious impact on artists and the broader Indian film industry. The request for safeguards affects not only the film fraternity but also every citizen who may be targeted by digital impersonation and deepfakes. Chiranjeevi believes that the government's willingness to listen is a positive sign that meaningful protections for creative professionals will be put in place. The actors emphasized that the threat to artists' dignity and rights must be addressed through stronger safeguards and strict legal penalties.

The articles provide background on Chiranjeevi, who is a Tollywood megastar and a former Union Minister, and his son, the actor Ram Charan. Chiranjeevi is currently filming an action family entertainer called Kaaka, which is directed by Bobby Kolli and features actress Anaswara Rajan. This upcoming movie also stars Nivetha Pethuraj, Anurag Kashyap, and Getup Srinu, and it is scheduled for release on January 13, 2027. Additionally, the actor has a socio-fantasy action thriller titled Vishwambhar in his pipeline, which is helmed by Mallidi Vassishta and stars Trisha Krishnan. These professional projects continue alongside his advocacy for the legal protection of artists against the dangers of modern artificial intelligence tools.

The government will now examine the submitted memorandum to determine how to introduce stronger safeguards and strict penalties for the misuse of AI. G. Kishan Reddy is responsible for coordinating the matter between the Union Home Ministry and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for review. The articles leave open whether the government will actually pass new laws or how the specific penalties for digital impersonation will look. It remains unclear when the government will provide a final response to the memorandum submitted by the actor on behalf of artists. The timeline for implementing these meaningful protections and the specific legal framework for the safeguards are not mentioned in the reports.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prepares for Nasdaq debut as Nvidia reports first earnings without Jensen Huang
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reports its first earnings without Jensen Huang on Tuesday, after his departure ended 33 years at the company he built. Interim CEO Colette Kress now faces investors at the world's most important AI hardware company. Anthropic is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Thursday at a valuation approaching $1.4 trillion. The offering could raise as much as $64.4 billion, one of the largest public offerings in market history. Wall Street had barely recovered from Huang's departure before this five-day stretch began.

Nvidia's market capitalisation fell from approximately $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion by Friday, nearly $2 trillion of shareholder wealth gone in a little over a month. The S&P 500 registered its first weekly gain after four consecutive declines and was up approximately 10.5% for the year. LSEG consensus cited in the market preview expects earnings growth of approximately 90% on quarterly revenue of $109 billion. Anthropic's latest prospectus outlined a transaction involving as many as 825 million shares and proceeds of up to $64.4 billion. Building a one-gigawatt data centre can cost at least $30 billion, and US technology companies have raised at least $220 billion through follow-on equity offerings this year, according to Bloomberg's compiled figures.

Colette Kress is described as an experienced executive with an intimate understanding of Nvidia's financial operations. Huang's influence extended beyond the usual responsibilities of a corporate CEO, as the industry's chief salesman, principal strategic negotiator and the man who could bring together customers, investors, infrastructure developers and technology suppliers. Nvidia reportedly took responsibility for the data-centre lease tied to Anthropic's reported $35 billion cloud-computing agreement with Nvidia-backed Lambda. The article asks whether new leadership will support customers and ecosystem partners with the same enthusiasm and whether it will become more conservative about strategic investments. It also asks whether regulatory scrutiny over semiconductor exports could make some of those relationships harder to maintain.

Bankers have discussed raising the offering price, and the order book is reportedly several times oversubscribed. Anthropic competes against OpenAI, Google and an increasingly capable collection of lower-cost open-weight models. Asia's semiconductor suppliers have considerable exposure to Nvidia's next move, the article states. The American consumer and the Fed have their own appointments with Wall Street next week, with retail sales, Fed minutes and a parade of consumer earnings on the calendar. The article says investors are increasingly distinguishing between the companies generating the AI spending and the businesses financing it.

Nvidia has become the unofficial central bank of the AI ecosystem, supplying chips, capital commitments and strategic relationships that helped finance an extraordinary infrastructure expansion. When capital was plentiful and GPU capacity scarce, the arrangement worked beautifully, letting Nvidia support selected customers and infrastructure partners and benefit from the resulting expansion in orders. Anthropic is preparing to test whether the public equity market will take on a much larger share of that financing burden. A successful listing could let Anthropic raise additional equity through follow-on offerings, issue convertible bonds, negotiate private placements or eventually access more conventional debt markets. Convertibles have become an important source of capital, allowing companies to borrow at relatively modest coupons while offering investors potential equity upside.

The article says the real test begins after the stabilisation bid disappears and shareholders discover that a $1.4 trillion valuation comes with a rather demanding earnings assignment. Unlike the private market, where valuations can remain insulated between financing rounds, public shareholders get to change their minds every trading session. The article leaves open whether the Bank of Nvidia intends to keep running the lending desk as aggressively without its chairman. It also leaves open how generous shareholders remain once the opening-day champagne runs out. The article states that the product road map is still intact and the hyperscalers are not about to stop building data centres because Huang is no longer wearing the leather jacket.

stories.Headline: China integrates artificial intelligence into education for 200 million students
stories.Summary:
China launched an ambitious nationwide drive to integrate artificial intelligence into education for almost 200 million students. This initiative aims to make AI literacy universal among schoolchildren from primary through secondary levels by 2030. The government seeks to produce a technologically skilled generation to ensure economic future and competition with the United States. A Reuters investigation found that the expansion remains uneven across schools, with no national agreement on teaching methods. The education ministry has encouraged schools to introduce AI courses and pilot programmes since 2024.

Beijing plans to establish 100 pilot demonstration schools and incorporate AI into student health monitoring. Shanghai requires at least 30 hours of annual AI teaching for each grade and deploys health monitoring systems. Ningxia and Gansu intend to introduce AI literacy into high-stakes school entrance examinations by 2027. Guizhou is incorporating behavioural analysis and facial recognition, while Yunnan will record 14,000 classrooms using AI. Beijing New Talent Academy charges $39,000 annually for 2,000 students on a 30-acre campus with a digital curriculum.

President Xi Jinping described AI education as fundamental to reform for the country's future economic success. Headmaster Yang Tianliang said AI agents guide students without fatigue and never make them feel stupid for asking. He attributed an increase in university admission rates from below 60 percent to 90 percent to AI. Peng Gaodi, a thirteen-year-old student, stated that AI noticeably improved his learning efficiency by helping him learn better. The education ministry did not respond to a Reuters request for comment regarding these nationwide educational initiatives.

Ted Mo Chen warned that children's thinking processes could be completely bypassed if they rely on AI for answers. Selena Guo stated that mature assessment rubrics for compulsory school-level AI competency are still being built by researchers. A study of 27,000 teenagers found an 18 percent homework score increase but a 20 percent exam decline. A survey of 320,000 pupils reported benefits alongside concerns about dependence and declining independent thinking and creative skills. Rural pupils may be particularly vulnerable to device addiction and cognitive outsourcing according to academic research.

Authorities committed at least $31 million over the past year to teacher training, educational platforms, and classroom AI equipment. Consultancy iResearch estimates that China's education digitalisation spending reached just under $83 billion in 2025. Generative AI projects accounted for 46 percent of AI education procurement during this period of rapid technological expansion. Funan County Qinqing High School in Anhui province uses models from Z.AI, ByteDance, and Alibaba's Qwen for lessons. This rural school serves 4,000 pupils, most of whom are children of migrant workers in the province.

Parents like Rita Luan are establishing limits by requiring children to attempt problems for 15 minutes before using AI. Peng Gaodi also attempts to solve coding problems himself before asking AI for hints rather than complete answers. The articles leave open how the government will eventually establish a national framework for assessing student AI literacy. It remains unclear how the government will address the decline in social science scores and independent thinking skills. The reports do not state when the proposed entrance examinations in Ningxia and Gansu will be finalized.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid scandal before Shenzhen Apec summit
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive of Nvidia on November 12. He left the company after reports revealed affairs with a female executive and a suspected Chinese spy. This scandal occurred just before a major CEO summit in Shenzhen, China. The event is hosted by the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum on November 17 and 18. These events have complicated the economic relationship between the United States and China.

The summit involves meetings between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and possibly Vladimir Putin on November 19. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will participate in a bilateral dialogue regarding artificial intelligence. The US has banned advanced AI chips, like the Blackwell, from reaching China. In January, the Trump administration allowed sales of the less powerful H200 chip to China. Oracle cancelled a US$7 billion contract giving Tencent access to AI chips in South-east Asia.

Chinese ambassador Xie Feng expressed high hopes for major-power cooperation at the Shenzhen summit. He promoted a China-led AI alliance called Waico to foster regional prosperity. President Xi Jinping has consistently described openness and cooperation as the way to achieve prosperity. He urged regional economies to keep global supply chains stable and avoid protectionism. The Communist Party publication Qiushi highlighted these themes through a series of previous Apec speeches.

China hawks in Congress are using the scandal to push three Bills restricting technology exports. US tech executives will likely press for more leniency for their companies in China. Some observers, including Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution, have low expectations for big changes. Paul Triolo noted that US cloud giants like Microsoft and Amazon could face scrutiny in 2027. Chris Miller stated that chip rules are more likely to tighten after the midterms.

China has required senior AI researchers at firms like Alibaba and DeepSeek to get travel approval. Regulators blocked SoftBank's US$5.4 billion acquisition of a robotics firm and ordered Meta to unwind a deal. The US provided over US$2.5 billion in loans to companies like MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. A trade truce from Busan, South Korea, saw tariffs fall to 30 per cent in May 2025. The countries also announced a 30-for-30 deal to lower barriers on US$30 billion of mutual exports.

The Busan agreement is set to expire on January 10, 2027, potentially resuming the trade war. The US may take new offensive measures, such as financial sanctions, against various Chinese companies. China could retaliate by restricting access to rare earths and powerful magnets used in fighter jets. Xi Jinping previously ordered military forces to be ready for a Taiwan invasion by 2027. Articles leave open whether a great power war or an AI-enabled cyberattack will occur.

stories.Headline: Nineye chief scientist Zhao Lu warns that AI code generation creates new security vulnerabilities
stories.Summary:
During the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, Zhao Lu addressed the growing risks of automated programming. He explained that large models are currently accelerating the speed of code generation across the globe. While these tools increase efficiency, ensuring the correctness and security of the resulting code remains a difficult challenge. This shift in how software is created has introduced significant vulnerabilities into the digital ecosystem.

The industry must now find new ways to secure open-source software as large models become more involved in coding. Previously, developers relied on manual audits to find errors and ensure the safety of their programs. They also utilized traditional static analysis and dynamic testing to maintain high security standards for their software. These older methods are no longer sufficient to handle the scale of AI-generated content.

Zhao Lu, who serves as the chief scientist at Nineye, highlighted these emerging threats during his presentation. He noted that the transition toward AI-driven development creates a new set of challenges for the entire technology industry. The responsibility for safety is shifting as the tools used to write code evolve rapidly. He emphasized that the industry must adapt its security protocols to keep pace with these advancements.

The current context involves a tension between the speed of AI production and the necessity of rigorous safety checks. As more companies integrate these large models, the risk of undetected bugs or security holes increases. The articles do not specify the exact next steps the industry will take to solve these problems. However, the discussion at the summit suggests that traditional auditing methods require urgent modernization.

stories.Headline: Apple asks developers to build Siri intents in iPhone apps for its 2027 smart glasses
stories.Summary:
On Sunday, November 15, 2026, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported in the "Power On" newsletter that Apple expects app developers to prepare for smart glasses due in 2027. Apple wants developers to focus on Siri integrations rather than apps running fully on the glasses, according to the report. The aim is for specific functions within apps to be accessible to Siri, which wearers then call upon by voice. AppleInsider and VR.org both covered the report, with VR.org's story by staff writer Jordan Kuo. Apple's first glasses will not run apps directly, and Apple wants developers to reach them through Siri AI integrations inside existing iPhone apps.

Apple still plans to announce the glasses at WWDC in June 2027, and shipments "would begin before the end of the year," with no augmented reality display. Prototypes codenamed N50 run a pared-down version of visionOS on a processor derived from Apple's older smartwatch chips and lean on a nearby iPhone for most functions. Wi-Fi keeps some functions outside third-party apps, such as audio playback, working after the wearer walks away from the phone. The frames are slightly thinner than Meta's second-generation Ray-Bans, with cameras sitting flush in oval openings on some test units, a front light for use and charging, and a magnetic charger Gurman describes as "roughly the size of a Tic Tac." On November 3 Apple opened Siri AI to all developers in the iOS 27.3 betas through a Developer Preview using App Intents, with App Store submission opening "in the spring."

Apple believes it has the upper hand on current market dominator Meta, because its advantage comes from its much larger pool of developers in the App Store. Apple had worked on Siri integrations for the iPhone long beforehand, so little effort should be needed to make those integrations work with the glasses. Apple's November 3 post says only that more details on "the terms and usage policies for experiences enabled through Siri AI" are coming. Apple says the API and Siri's behavior may change during the preview, so the background-name rule is current rather than final. Apple does not sell HomeView in the European Union, "as Siri AI is currently unavailable in iOS in the EU," and says it is "working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward."

AppleInsider compares the plan to HomeView, the $299 home screen Apple put on sale November 13, which has no App Store and plays compatible third-party audio and video apps. A footnote in Apple's October announcement says select apps "require a paired and compatible iPhone nearby," and MacRumors traced those to CarPlay-enabled apps through the Apple Developer Program agreement. Commenters on the AppleInsider article raised prescription lenses, with one saying 70% of people use them and 10% more need them but do not use them yet, leaving only 20% of the market. Meta's Wearables Device Access Toolkit hands an iOS or Android app the glasses' camera, microphones and audio, and Google describes its glasses experiences as "a dedicated activity that runs within your phone's existing app." Meta's toolkit was tagged 1.0.1 on October 9 in its iOS repository, and its FAQ still says developers will "soon" be able to submit experiences for publishing, with no date attached.

The first Apple Watch apps in 2015 ran their code as WatchKit extensions on the paired iPhone, and native watch apps waited for watchOS 2 that September. Apple made a similar plea to developers to work on elements before the launch of the Apple Vision Pro. Google's projected activities give an app a surface of its own, on a Jetpack Projected library still at 1.0.0-alpha14, ahead of the Intelligent Eyewear frames that ship December 10. Google's docs say the XR_PROJECTED_LAUNCHER category exists so Gemini can find a projected activity when "a user issues a voice command using the app's name." Apple Intelligence features that rely on server-side models, Siri AI among them, are subject to daily usage limits, with expanded access "available for a fee in the future."

People can leave an app's name out of a request only while that app is in the foreground, while it has a Live Activity running, or when they continue a Siri conversation that already mentioned it. Otherwise, "while your app is in the background, requests need to mention your app," which on glasses whose phone stays in a pocket means the wearer says the app's name or the developer keeps a Live Activity going. Siri shows an app's custom content as a card snippet built from the developer's own SwiftUI view, and the first glasses have no display. Apple ships a Siri Integration Advisor in Xcode and a Siri Evaluations framework that scripts conversations with Siri and catches it when Siri starts handling intents differently. Nothing reported so far says whether third-party apps will get the camera at all.

stories.Headline: Timirah and Mia James found Sonic Intelligence Academy to hold first AI Music Awards
stories.Summary:
The Sonic Intelligence Academy held the first AI Music Awards on Friday, November 14, 2026, at the Mayan Theater in Downtown Los Angeles. Software engineer Timirah James and her sister Mia James created the organization to normalize tech-assisted tunes and support AI creators. The event featured a red carpet with human creators and a text-to-speech agent developed by the top sponsor, Deepgram. Xania Monet won both artist and song of the year, while DJ Shawn Q took the producer of the year award. Telisha Jones, the human behind Xania Monet, had previously won the AI Album of the Year at a summit.

Artists must register tracks to the Verified Registry to specify if songs are fully AI-generated, AI-assisted, or human and AI hybrids. Registered artists nominate peers and vote across 25 categories, including Best AI Pop Song and Best AI Comedic Song. The organization launched its own AI charts in January 2026 to counter the mainstream industry and the Recording Academy. The event started at 6:45 p.m., thirty minutes after the scheduled 6:15 p.m. start, and featured a house band.

The Mayan Theater is located a twelve minute walk from the Crypto.com Arena, which is the longtime home of the Grammys. Timirah James and Mia James founded the academy to provide infrastructure for AI music rather than dismissing its existence. They advocate for artists to publicly associate themselves with AI-powered work to highlight the humans who helped create the product. Xania Monet creator Telisha Jones stated that AI is just a tool that emphasizes what creators do. Fredro Starr, who debuted the moniker Mad AI, claimed humans cannot be replaced and bring the spirit of hip-hop.

He touted his record, It All Started in Brooklyn, as the first AI album released on vinyl. The event affected nominees who missed hearing their names called because the show skipped introductions for the first half of awards. Guests included actor Giovanni Wilson and podcast host Lana Hout, who both served as hosts for the chaotic evening. Media coverage included twelve independent ventures on the carpet, though twenty-nine outlets had signed up before a flight ground-stop.

The company Trinity Social ran an ad featuring a Rockstar Games logo, which a Rockstar spokesperson did not authorize. Some industry figures, including Kehlani, previously criticized the three million dollar record deal received by Telisha Jones. The academy was launched in January to counter the music industry's aversion to AI and the legal questions surrounding copyright infringement. Lawsuits have been filed by record labels and artists against AI generators such as Udio and Suno over these issues.

The event used a Claude-generated run-of-show on a teleprompter that shifted rapidly and confused the hosts during the ceremony. A trailer for the film A Good Hand Wasted, starring Terrance Howard, was played but only showed a small portion. The evening was marked by technical failures, including a Deepgram AI voice that talked over the presenters. The hosts eventually presented the best AI country artist award thirteen minutes late after a confusing interruption regarding a commercial break.

The event ended with various technical kinks, such as the teleprompter acting erratically and the Deepgram commercials playing at random moments. The articles do not state if the Sonic Intelligence Academy will hold a second annual awards show in the future. It remains unclear if Rockstar Games will take legal action regarding the unauthorized use of its logo in the advertisement. The text leaves open whether the industry will eventually accept AI-generated music on the standard Billboard charting positions.

stories.Headline: Trump avoids discussing Nvidia scandal during upcoming summit with Xi Jinping
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump is not expected to raise the Nvidia scandal with President Xi Jinping next week. The controversy involves former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his affair with a suspected Chinese spy. U.S. officials say this matter should not affect the upcoming summit between the two leaders. The administration intends to keep the national security issue separate from their diplomatic discussions. This decision follows reports that Huang resigned as chief executive amid the spying allegations.

Trump will visit Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, for the APEC summit on November 18 and 19. He meets Xi on November 19 and will also attend a trilateral summit with Vladimir Putin. The scandal involves Alice Huang, a former senior executive at the Singaporean company Megaspeed International. Megaspeed is suspected of shipping advanced AI chips to China to circumvent U.S. export controls. The U.S. government maintains that semiconductor export controls are not subject to negotiation with China.

A senior U.S. official stated that export controls are national security matters decided through interagency consultation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Treasury, State, and Defense departments supported designating Megaspeed months ago. Bessent expressed frustration that the Commerce Department, which holds final authority, delayed adding Megaspeed to the list. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces questions regarding his responsibility for this delay in the export process. The U.S. government reaffirms it will not use chip restrictions as bargaining chips in trade talks.

Congressional Democrats wrote to Howard Lutnick demanding an immediate halt to advanced AI chip exports to China. Lawmakers from both parties are pressing for tougher legislation to protect the American technological edge. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning called the spy narratives fabricated pretexts for imposing technology restrictions. Beijing has refuted the claims about Alice Huang, calling the allegations unsubstantiated and completely unfounded. Analysts suggest the scandal provides China hawks in Congress a specific story to support tighter controls.

Nvidia once held 95 percent of the Chinese market before restrictions applied during the Biden administration. Trump previously allowed Nvidia to sell H200 chips in China despite security concerns over advanced technology. U.S. intelligence suspects Alice Huang was recruited to influence Nvidia to make cutting-edge chips more available. The U.S. Justice Department has not yet concluded if Alice Huang actually acted for Beijing. The U.S. and China have previously committed to creating a hotline for AI security incidents.

The Trump administration is weighing ways to close loopholes, including tightening licensing and restricting remote chip access. A Senate defense policy bill may authorize Congress to review licenses and track chips to prevent diversion. The U.S. may also compel allies to match its restrictions on exports to Chinese chipmakers. It remains open whether Beijing will separate export controls from broader AI safety discussions during talks. The articles leave uncertain if the U.S. will face retaliation for closing existing chip loopholes.

stories.Headline: OECD reports AI adoption accelerates across member countries but gaps persist among businesses and generations
stories.Summary:
The OECD reported on 5 November 2026 that AI adoption is accelerating across its member countries, but that major gaps persist among businesses and between generations. The organisation said the world of work is changing rapidly because of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, along with new forms of work, greening, demographic change and globalisation. It also said critical minerals have become central to economic security, as they are essential to energy and digital transitions, defence and advanced manufacturing. The OECD published the findings on its website as part of its work on effective governance to harness the benefits of AI and mitigate its risks. The OECD said its work on investment supports governments in attracting more and better-quality investment, with priority given to security and sustainability.

It also described how the trend towards the international dispersion of certain value chain activities produces challenges, and said it offers policies to meet these. The organisation noted that its Programme for International Student Assessment, known as PISA, assesses the skills of 15-year-old students in reading, mathematics and science as core domains. The articles give no further figures, dates or names beyond these. The OECD is responsible for the work described, and its statements were paraphrased in the articles rather than attributed to a named individual. The organisation framed the findings around applying effective governance to harness the benefits of AI and mitigate its risks.

It presented the changing world of work as a result of new technologies, new forms of work, greening, demographic change and globalisation. It did not say in the articles what specific measures it recommends or who should carry them out. The context given is that AI adoption is spreading quickly across OECD countries while gaps remain among businesses and generations. The articles do not say what happens next, beyond the OECD's stated focus on governance and on attracting better-quality investment. No further steps, deadlines or responses are reported.

stories.Headline: Reuters finds 3.2 billion dollars in restricted Nvidia chips used for Chinese AI projects
stories.Summary:
Reuters published an investigation on November 13, 2026, regarding restricted Nvidia chips in China. The report found over 150 Chinese contracts worth 3.2 billion dollars for AI projects. These projects utilized restricted processors including H100, H200, and H800 chips. This discovery happened the same week CBS News reported on Jensen Huang resigning as chief executive. The investigation revealed that Chinese demand for Nvidia hardware continued despite official company guidance.

The projects involve 23 billion yuan in spending on AI computing and supporting infrastructure. In 2025, Huang stated that Nvidia market share in China fell from 95 percent to zero. During Q3 FY2026, the company called H20 sales insignificant, and Q1 FY2027 shipments were zero. This compared to 4.6 billion dollars in shipments from the previous year. IDC estimates Nvidia held 34 percent of Chinese AI accelerator shipments in early 2026.

CFO Collette Kress stated on August 26 that forward outlooks include no China data center compute revenue. She noted that Hopper 200 shipments to China were dilutive to corporate gross margins. Jensen Huang said that unconstrained demand would be a lot higher than the 70 percent delivered. He also stated that compute is revenue while discussing fiscal 2028 and current supply levels. Kress has now stepped in as the interim CEO following the resignation of Huang.

The report affects Chinese projects that Reuters says are now imperiled by U.S. scrutiny. Analysts like Dan Ives and Bessent questioned if the company truly knew its customers. Some believe the entire AI economy is built on top of Nvidia and its leadership. Rebecca Bellan noted that the resignation restored her faith in humanity regarding billionaire behavior. Others worry that loosening chip exports to China creates a significant national security issue.

Huang resigned after reports of an affair with an executive at a customer called Megaspeed. This individual is alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence, which the board is investigating. There was also a reported affair between Huang and another executive within the Nvidia company. Intelligence circles and the government reportedly knew about the Alice Huang relationship for nearly a year. Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not seem to mind the situation.

Nvidia will now be managed by Collette Kress as a caretaker while the board figures things out. The company faces export control risks since it told investors to expect zero revenue from China. Q3 guidance of 108 billion dollars assumes no China data center compute revenue for the firm. The articles leave open whether the board probe will lead to further leadership changes. It remains unclear how U.S. scrutiny will impact the existing restricted chips inside Chinese projects.

stories.Headline: US officials probe Alibaba for providing cloud access to restricted Nvidia AI chips
stories.Summary:
US officials launched a fresh regulatory probe into Alibaba Group Holding on November 15, 2026. The investigation focuses on allegations involving the CEO of Nvidia and various Alibaba cloud partners. Regulators are reviewing claims that Alibaba linked data centers provided remote access to advanced AI chips. These specific Nvidia processors are currently subject to strict US export controls. The probe examines if cloud access allowed Chinese clients to use restricted hardware.

The investigation looks at whether cloud access bypassed the need for direct chip shipments to China. This scrutiny affects Alibaba Cloud, which provides infrastructure for merchants and enterprises in China and abroad. The company has a three year AI and cloud capex plan totaling RMB 380b. T Head has shipped 470,000 AI chips as part of this broader technology strategy. Alibaba also targets an ARR of RMB 16b plus for model and application services during 2026.

US regulators are responsible for the probe and are examining the company's cloud relationships. They are reviewing whether remote access to restricted Nvidia processors violated existing export rules. Officials are investigating if these arrangements allowed restricted AI hardware to reach Chinese users. The regulators want to know if cloud-based access served as a loophole for shipments. This scrutiny targets the link between Alibaba's technology capabilities and its retail platform.

Business customers using Alibaba's core cloud services are affected by this potential loss of hardware. If regulators close remote access, Alibaba may need to rework how AI workloads are provisioned. The company might have to adjust which customers it serves from specific data centers. This could lead to higher operational costs or lower performance for some cloud services. Such restrictions could also slow the payback on the company's massive AI capex spending.

Alibaba runs a large commerce ecosystem and provides cloud infrastructure for many global enterprises. The company's current narrative relies on turning AI investments into profitable model and cloud services. T Head is a key part of this strategy through its AI chip shipments. The company is currently working toward a fair value of 186 dollars. AI lab losses and negative free cash flow remain central points of financial focus.

Investors should watch for explicit commentary on US export rules in upcoming quarterly reports. Disclosure in T Head Hong Kong listing documents will provide early signals on the issue. These documents may quantify changes to AI related capex plans or chip sourcing strategies. The articles leave open whether regulators will actually block remote access to Nvidia processors. It remains unclear if Alibaba can maintain its ARR targets under tighter US rules.

stories.Headline: Apple launches HomeView with Siri AI and confirms a December update for voice door unlocks
stories.Summary:
Apple began selling its HomeView product on Friday, November 13, 2026, to serve as a center for the home. The company describes this new device as an artificial intelligence powered product designed for household connectivity and control. It features a seven inch Liquid Retina display and a twelve megapixel Center Stage camera for user recognition. Users can place the device on a tabletop or mount it on a wall for their convenience. The system is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI to help customers manage their smart home.

The device costs 299 dollars, though wall mounted setups start from 358.95 dollars, and it is not sold in the EU. It recognizes six people by face and voice to show personal content from Messages, Calendar, and other relevant information. HomeView ships with software version 26.5 and prompts users to update to version 27.2, which was released November 12. It uses an A18 chip to lock camera and microphone data so that it is never shared with Apple. The device works with the Home app to manage settings, automations, and various smart home accessories.

Greg Joswiak, senior vice president of worldwide marketing, said the device keeps households better connected and informed via Siri AI. Executive Chair Tim Cook posted on X that the product provides intelligence, entertainment, and connection personal to every user. Kaiann Drance, vice president of product marketing for home, stated that Siri AI allows for a previously impossible experience. Lilian Rincon, vice president of product marketing for AI, described the new version of the digital assistant as much more capable. An Apple spokesperson told Joanna Stern that recognized users can already unlock doors using the on screen interface.

Reviewer Joanna Stern found that Siri AI refused to unlock her front door or garage door and claimed it had no camera. Some X users called it the worst piece of tech they ever purchased, citing a schizophrenic Siri with multiple voices. Other affected buyers reported that the device is glitchy, unable to open apps, or unable to play music via Apple Music. One user shared a video of a song glitching and argued that the 299 dollar device should just work. These users experienced technical issues with pictures and music, and some found that Apple support had no answers.

Reports from July indicated that Apple was preparing a major push into the smart home product and software market. This move puts Apple in closer competition with the Google Nest Hub and the Amazon Echo as AI advances. A March PYMNTS Intelligence report found that 54 percent of U.S. adults were using AI for personal tasks. Researchers in Tokyo and Michigan previously showed that light aimed at microphones could inject voice commands into older Siri devices. Those researchers noted that attackers could potentially brute force a smart lock PIN or open garage doors using such methods.

Apple confirmed a December 2026 update will extend voice control to security accessories once the HomeView recognizes the person asking. The company has not yet provided a specific release day or a version number for this upcoming December software update. Users must currently use the touchscreen or the Home app for locks and garage doors until the voice fix arrives. It remains open whether the update will require a recognized voice, a recognized face, or both to open doors. The articles leave open if a paired device must also vouch for the person to ensure secure voice unlocking.

stories.Headline: 42Gears earns ISO/IEC 42001 certification for its AI management system
stories.Summary:
42Gears announced on November 13, 2026, that it had achieved certification to ISO/IEC 42001:2023, the international standard for Artificial Intelligence Management Systems. The company said the certification followed a rigorous independent audit conducted by the British Standards Institution, known as BSI. 42Gears described itself as a global leader in Unified Endpoint Management, or UEM. The announcement was issued from Bengaluru, in Karnataka, India, according to the article. The certification recognizes 42Gears for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving structured governance across its AI-enabled enterprise capabilities.

The certification covers 42Gears' role as a producer, provider, and user of AI systems integrated within its flagship SureMDM platform. That role includes the use of third-party large language models, or LLMs, to deliver AI-powered unified endpoint management services. The services reach key global sectors including Banking and Financial Services, Healthcare and Life Sciences, Industrial and Supply Chain Operations, and Consumer and Commercial Services. The certification complements 42Gears' existing compliance portfolio, which includes ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, and HIPAA programs. 42Gears products are used by more than 23,000 customers across more than 170 countries and are available through more than 1,000 global partners.

Onkar Singh, Co-founder and CEO of 42Gears, said enterprise IT teams want the efficiency and intelligence of AI but not at the expense of security, transparency, or regulatory compliance. He said the ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification validates the company's commitment to responsible AI innovation. He said customers in banking, healthcare, and mission-critical operations can deploy SureMDM's AI capabilities knowing they are backed by internationally audited governance and strict human oversight. The article said the certification demonstrates that 42Gears embeds accountability, transparency, and human oversight across the AI lifecycle. It said the company establishes robust governance frameworks for the responsible development, deployment, and use of AI technologies, including the adoption and use of LLMs.

The article listed benefits for 42Gears customers and partners, starting with independently audited AI governance that provides verified assurance that SureMDM's AI management framework meets rigorous international compliance benchmarks. It described an end-to-end risk and impact assessment that establishes a structured methodology for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating AI-related risks across the entire deployment lifecycle. It said transparency and human oversight enforce clear accountability mechanisms and human oversight controls over AI-assisted decision-making and workflows. It said governed third-party LLM integration ensures strict security, privacy, and vendor oversight protocols when leveraging external large language models. It said the comprehensive compliance posture offers heightened confidence for organizations operating in heavily regulated industries.

The second article reported that New Relic published its 2026 Impact Report on September 29, 2026, and became the first observability provider to earn ISO/IEC 42001 certification. New Relic said the certification signifies that an independent, accredited third party audited and verified its internal Artificial Intelligence Management System for responsible, ethical, and transparent AI governance across its entire lifecycle. The company published its public AI Principles and joined the EU AI Pact to align proactively with the EU AI Act ahead of formal enforcement. Through strict tool vetting and updated risk frameworks, New Relic said it meets rigorous global standards for data safety and oversight. The report said this transforms AI governance from static policy into active, platform-wide accountability.

New Relic's GreenOps program generated approximately $18 million in cost savings in FY26, surpassing its $15 million target, driven by over 80 targeted engineering initiatives including architectural right-sizing and data archiving. The program cut cloud carbon emissions by 10 to 12 percent per unit of work. New Relic said it modernized its infrastructure to curb carbon intensity as compute demands scale. The report also covered the expansion of the company's Enterprise Risk Management framework. The article said New Relic pairs responsible AI governance with sustainable operational growth.
