stories.Headline: Rajnath Singh urges AI and robotics integration in defence testing to boost self-reliance
stories.Summary:
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged greater use of artificial intelligence, machine learning and robotics in Non-Destructive Testing, TechGig reported on November 15, 2026. He spoke virtually at a three-day conference organised by the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing in Hyderabad. The TechGig report was published on November 15, 2026 at 09:54 PM IST. Singh called for integrating these technologies to boost India's defence capabilities and strategic self-reliance. He said technological innovation is crucial for strengthening the nation's defence ecosystem.

Singh addressed the joint inauguration of the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation and Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace. More than 2,000 industry leaders, researchers and professionals gathered in Hyderabad for the event, Pragativadi reported on November 15, 2026. Singh said India must move from being a mere consumer of advanced technologies to becoming a global developer, innovator and leader in critical domains. He called for rapid domestic development in specialised sensors, evaluation equipment and associated software to secure critical supply chains. He said there can be zero compromise on the integrity of testing results in strategic applications.

Singh said India's pursuit of Aatmanirbharta in defence is not merely an economic objective but also a strategic necessity. He warned that hidden defects can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce service life and jeopardise mission success. He said the sector needs to move beyond merely identifying defects towards preventing them by embedding quality at every stage of manufacturing. He praised government catalysts such as Innovations for Defence Excellence and the Technology Development Fund. He called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-ecosystem approach uniting public sector undertakings, private manufacturers, start-ups, MSMEs, academia and research laboratories.

Singh said AI, ML, robotics, advanced sensors, digital twins and predictive analytics are expanding the possibilities of inspection and structural health monitoring. He said these technologies can improve inspection speed and consistency, facilitate complex data analysis and help identify defects conventional methods might miss. He urged NDT professionals to continuously upgrade their skills and embrace innovation in line with emerging technologies and evolving security requirements. He advocated greater indigenous innovation, urging India to develop solutions tailored to its strategic and industrial needs rather than merely adopting emerging technologies. He said investment in research, advanced equipment, software and skilled manpower would strengthen domestic capabilities and help Indian technologies access international markets.

Singh used a medical analogy, explaining that just as X-rays and ultrasounds examine the human body without surgery, NDT allows engineers to inspect vital defence hardware without dismantling or damaging it. He said this hardware includes missiles, naval vessels and spacecraft. He noted that India's indigenous arsenal is growing more sophisticated, exemplified by milestones like the aircraft carrier INS Vikrant and advancements in radar and missile systems. He said testing protocols must evolve as a result. The three-day conference in Hyderabad continues to serve as a hub for technical deliberation, fostering partnerships aimed at future-proofing India's aerospace and defence manufacturing sectors.

The articles do not state what specific policy changes, funding commitments or timelines, if any, follow from Singh's remarks. They do not say whether the government will mandate AI, ML or robotics in defence NDT or set targets for indigenous adoption. They do not name the specific officials, PSUs, start-ups or institutions that would take part in the proposed whole-of-ecosystem approach. They do not give the conference's closing date or any outcomes expected from it. They do not say how Indian testing technologies would access international markets or what barriers currently exist.

stories.Headline: AC Milan appoints Rúben Amorim as head coach as AI posts falsely claim Paolo Maldini returns
stories.Summary:
Recent national headlines warned that New Orleans was replacing 911 professionals with AI, and the reports were wrong, but the misinformation spread quickly amid the firestorm surrounding this new technology. The U.S. is not handing its emergency response system over to computers, and AI is making emergency communications faster and more resilient while trained 911 professionals remain in charge. Viral posts on Instagram and Threads claimed that AC Milan legend Paolo Maldini had returned to the club as head coach of its men's first team. The posts were designed to resemble genuine football transfer and appointment announcements, complete with the familiar excitement of a "Here we go!" update.

The creators included a disclaimer reading "CONCEPT ART • AI | FICTIONAL SCENARIO," indicating that the announcement is an AI-generated concept rather than an actual development. AI can identify and translate other languages almost instantly, whereas bringing a human translator on the line takes precious minutes, and it can support realistic training simulations that better equip new hires for the demands of the job. It can analyze far more calls for quality assurance than supervisors could review manually, helping ensure call-takers perform at their best. AI can also help relieve the burden of routine, non-emergency calls coming to 911 centers, roughly two-thirds of all calls handled by 911 centers according to the 2025 Pulse of 911 survey, freeing telecommunicators to focus on calls where lives are on the line. The Enhancing First Response Act (S. 725) would correct the longstanding federal misclassification of 911 telecommunicators as secretarial and administrative personnel rather than the protective service professionals they truly are.

Having passed the Senate unanimously, the legislation now awaits action in the House, and Congress should encourage responsible innovation by passing bipartisan funding legislation to support the nationwide transition to an all-digital Next Generation 911 system. John Provenzano is CEO of NENA: The 9-1-1 Association, a nonprofit professional organization representing tens of thousands of 9-1-1 first responders across the U.S. He wrote that emergency calls are not ordinary customer-service transactions and that 911 has always depended on a direct personal connection. He said someone reporting a heart attack, hiding from an attacker, or helping an injured child may need calm reassurance, lifesaving instructions, or sound judgment amid confusion and changing facts. He wrote that human intuition and empathy are essential features of 911 that AI cannot replace, and that AI will not change the fundamental social contract that has existed since the beginning: when a citizen calls for help, 911 will answer. He called on Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.)

to bring the bill up for consideration during the lame-duck session under suspension of the rules. Provenzano wrote that the question is not whether AI is categorically "dangerous" or "safe" but whether we can harness its potential while ensuring the safety, reliability, privacy and public trust that underpin emergency response. He wrote that realizing that promise will require thoughtful implementation, clear standards and continued investment in both people and infrastructure. The football article said that with realistic-looking graphics and the emotional appeal of a legendary football figure returning home, such posts can easily confuse fans who come across them while scrolling through their feeds.

It said that for supporters who are emotionally invested in their clubs, the prospect of a beloved former player returning to the dugout can be particularly tempting to believe. It said that a quick check of official club announcements and credible sports publications can save fans from falling for an elaborate digital prank. Provenzano wrote that the 911 system Americans rely on today has come a long way since the first call made nearly 60 years ago. He wrote that over the decades 911 has repeatedly adopted new technologies to better serve the public, from mobile phones and text messages to digital data-sharing and streaming video, and that the system has evolved alongside Americans' technology preferences.

He wrote that AI is the next step in this evolution and that the industry's experience in safely implementing previous technologies will guide it now. AC Milan officially appointed Portuguese manager Rúben Amorim as head coach of its men's first team on June 16, 2026, following the departure of Massimiliano Allegri. The former Manchester United and Sporting CP manager was welcomed by the Italian club as part of its plans to rebuild the team. Paolo Maldini has never pursued a coaching career, and after hanging up his boots he remained associated with AC Milan in an administrative capacity, serving as the club's technical director until June 2023.

He also briefly took up the role of technical director at the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) in July 2026, but resigned after just 16 days. The football article said that AI-generated content is increasingly blurring the lines between football news and digital fiction, and that fabricated stories can acquire the appearance of genuine breaking news. It said that while AI can recreate the excitement of a dream managerial appointment, it cannot make that appointment real. It said that Maldini's return to AC Milan might make for a wonderful fictional football story, but Amorim is the man in the hot seat.

stories.Headline: Anthropic launches Nasdaq IPO to fund frontier models amid AI industry backlash
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is launching an initial public offering on the Nasdaq this Thursday, November 19, 2026, to raise money for its frontier models. The company is going public during a difficult period for the technology industry, which is currently facing a nationwide artificial intelligence backlash. This event follows a major political shift in Washington, D.C., and the sudden ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang early Thursday. The IPO arrives as investors seek a bright spot after the Nasdaq dropped 5.3 percent in October, its worst month since March 2025. This offering is considered a defining event for the young artificial intelligence market and the most important tech IPO in several years.

The IPO price is expected between 70 and 78 dollars a share, with a valuation of 1.4 trillion dollars and six times oversubscription. Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, Micron, Broadcom, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, and Advanced Micro Devices are collectively investing 26 billion dollars at this price. Anthropic has 900 billion dollars in spending commitments, including 110 billion dollars over ten years with Amazon and 400 billion dollars for cloud capacity. The lab committed 300 billion dollars to chip and data center partners and 125 billion to 150 billion dollars for Google chips. Google will own 13 percent of the company and backstop 19 billion dollars in lease commitments to Terawulf for Kentucky data centers.

Anthropic stated in its prospectus that it previously underestimated compute requirements, which constrained its capacity and impacted both product development and deployment. The company recorded a net loss of 104 billion dollars through the first nine months of 2026 before this public offering. Joe Fath of Eclipse called the staggering numbers hard to wrap one's head around, while David Tollen called it smart investing. Subhadeep Chatterjee, a former Google cloud partnerships leader, stated that everyone knows Anthropic is going to be the future of Google. Eli Mansoor of OskaQ Consulting said companies must rush to get infrastructure or they will be out of business.

The IPO affects major tech giants who need Anthropic's massive spending to continue for many years to come to drive the AI buildout. Corey Quinn of Duckbill said it is almost certain that the ten year Amazon contract will be renegotiated before it culminates. Investors are currently strained by rising interest rates, which have pushed them out of debt heavy neoclouds that are critical for infrastructure. Democratic victories in midterm elections and new ballot measures may potentially limit the development of new data centers across the country. Nvidia shareholders are affected as shares tumbled 13 percent this week to their lowest levels since July 2025 following the scandal.

Anthropic is a five year old company that has never lived through a technology downturn but is now burning historic amounts of money. The company has 132 billion dollars in existing cash and short term investments and could yield over 90 billion dollars in proceeds. Amazon previously built a custom chip data center in Indiana specifically for Anthropic, while cloud partners account for 31 percent of obligations. Bank of America, Blackstone, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley offered 63 billion dollars to buy Broadcom AI chip racks for Anthropic to rent. Broadcom has provided a backstop for these rentals with a maximum liability of 43 billion dollars to support the lab.

Nvidia interim CEO Colette Cress faces a major test on Tuesday when the company reports quarterly results two days before the Anthropic debut. A data center for Anthropic that starts leasing in 2027 has a unique twenty year term to ensure future computing capacity. The articles leave open whether the explosive growth of the company can outpace its massive expenses as Jim Cramer questioned. It remains uncertain if the AI trade will be revived or if Nvidia's competitors will capture a greater share of the market. The market is still tracking three scenarios to determine how the artificial intelligence trade will be resolved in the coming months.

stories.Headline: Character.ai files for bankruptcy as Ollie and Sora shut down
stories.Summary:
Character.ai filed for bankruptcy in October 2026, while the privacy assistant Ollie ceased operations a few weeks before that date. Many other projects failed, including the video platform Sora, which shut down in March 2026 due to high costs. The workflow tool Relay closed in August 2026, and Notion Mail is scheduled to shut down on September 22. Humane closed its AI Pin business in February 2025, and the browser ChatGPT Atlas ended on August 9.

The Character.ai sale to Disney involves a bid of 20 million dollars for certain intellectual property rights. Apple paid a 250 million dollar settlement after delaying the Siri AI upgrade, which finally appeared in iOS 27. Humane raised 230 million dollars before HP acquired most of its assets for 116 million dollars in February 2025. Character.ai previously raised 150 million dollars in 2023 and received 2.7 billion dollars from Google for technology licensing. The Rabbit R1 device debuted at CES in January 2024 and reportedly sold 100,000 units shortly after launch.

S&P Global Market Intelligence reports that 42 percent of AI projects fail because of funding or weak user demand. CEO Bill Lennon stated that Ollie would shut down on November 6 due to slow growth and funding issues. OpenAI rolled back a July 9 redesign of ChatGPT after users called the new interface confusing and cluttered. Microsoft delayed its Recall feature for nearly a year to reassess security safeguards after receiving strong privacy backlash. Apple cited engineering issues and bugs as the reasons for the repeated delays of its upgraded Siri AI.

Users of ChatGPT criticized the super app redesign, and families sued Character.ai over teen suicides and self-harm. Disney issued cease and desist letters to Character.ai, and customers were warned that Humane charging cases might catch fire. Cybersecurity researchers affected Microsoft by creating a tool that could extract sensitive data captured by the Recall photographic memory. Notion Mail users were already using standalone AI agents, which made the dedicated email product unnecessary for the market. Rabbit R1 users found the device to be unfinished and unstable according to early reviews of the hardware.

S&P Global notes that technical challenges, intense competition, and scaling difficulties contribute to the growing cemetery of failed AI projects. Character.ai was founded in 2021 by former Google researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas to create customizable bots. Ollie launched in June 2026 as a family assistant and was among the first mainstream apps with SOC 2. Relay operated for five years as a Zapier alternative before major platforms integrated similar automation features into their tools. Microsoft introduced Recall at the 2024 Build developer conference to allow users to search their digital history via screenshots.

The Character.ai transaction with Disney is expected to be completed by late November or early December of the year 2026. Siri AI is currently being rolled out to English users, with support for additional languages expected to follow soon. CFT regulations may influence the future viability of AI projects, though the articles do not specify the exact rules. The articles leave open whether Microsoft has truly fixed the underlying security issues regarding the controversial Recall memory feature. It remains unclear if the Rabbit R1 will be updated to fix the unstable performance noted by early reviewers.

stories.Headline: Pedro Pascal says filming Behemoth! gives him hope amid the AI boom
stories.Summary:
Tony Gilroy wrote and directed the Searchlight film Behemoth!, which stars Pedro Pascal and premieres in theaters on December 4. The movie focuses on a fight for humanity and explores if artificial intelligence can replace the humanizing element of cinema. Pascal plays Alex Serian, a former child prodigy cellist who returns home to Los Angeles to compose film scores. This story also follows the main character as he attempts to reconnect with his family through his musical work. The production serves as a lyrical love letter to the music of the movies according to a review.

The film features a cast including Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Will Arnett, Hank Azaria, Margarita Levieva, and Matthew Lillard. It requires a focus on organic storytelling to push back against the current boom of artificial intelligence in art. The plot centers on the city of Los Angeles where the protagonist returns to pursue his professional composing career. Searchlight Pictures is the studio responsible for releasing the movie on the specific date of December 4. Every department involved in the film worked with a purity of love despite not making money on the project.

Pedro Pascal told Vanity Fair that the experience of shooting the movie injected him with a tremendous amount of hope. He noted that the most expensive people were involved because of their talent and experience rather than for profit. Pascal believes there is a thrilling pushback occurring this year through movies that fight for humanity and storytelling. He stated that people want to be connected, tell each other's stories, and look after one another as humans. The actor was surprised that Gilroy made the film so intimate and healing instead of being mean.

Tony Gilroy stated that there is a clear natural resistance to the robot takeover in the music and film industries. He believes that people want humans and noted that the music scene has been dying for fifteen years. Gilroy suggested that people should blow up AI centers at the voting box by going and voting against them. He admitted that an algorithm could probably replace the emotional amplitude of movies, but this specific film is organic. The director is a two time Oscar nominee who champions the humanity of art over an over-reliance on AI.

The articles explain that the music scene has been struggling for fifteen years but is now grooving a little bit. This background sets the stage for a film that emphasizes organic human connection over the efficiency of artificial intelligence. The production involved highly experienced talent who worked together in a contagious environment of love for the creative process. The film was screened at the New York Film Festival where it received a positive lyrical review. These elements combine to create a project that resists the current trend of using AI in the arts.

The movie will officially premiere in theaters on December 4 to bring its message of humanity to the general public. Future developments regarding the fight for creativity and politics in cinema remain open as the AI boom continues growing. It is unclear what will happen next in the industry or what specific elements of cinema will return. The articles leave open whether the pushback against AI will successfully protect the humanizing elements of the movie business. The long term impact of this organic approach to filmmaking remains to be seen after the premiere.

stories.Headline: Anthropic ports AI model to AMD hardware in three days to reduce reliance on Nvidia software
stories.Summary:
Anthropic recently announced that its AI model could be ported to different hardware in just three days. This development occurred around November 15, 2026, and provides a major advantage to Advanced Micro Devices. The move potentially weakens the market dominance of Nvidia by reducing the reliance on its software. This shift allows AI labs to switch chip vendors much faster than was previously possible.

The process involved the Claude Mythos Preview model porting 100 percent of its kernels to AMD MI355 GPUs. This replaces a traditional process requiring twelve engineers and between six and twelve months of work. Anthropic aims to create a fungible compute pool using AMD, Nvidia, Amazon Trainium, and Alphabet Tensor Processing Units. AMD's Helios system costs roughly 20 billion dollars per gigawatt, while Nvidia's Vera Rubin costs 40 billion.

Anthropic stated that its goal was to bring any AI chip up to speed within a few days. The company wants to buy chips based on the best price performance regardless of the specific vendor. This strategy allows the lab to use different chips for model training or inference based on efficiency. By reducing the complexity of switching hardware, the company levels the playing field for semiconductor manufacturers.

Investors in AMD may benefit, while Nvidia faces potential losses in sales, gross margins, and overall profitability. The shift affects the semiconductor space by challenging the moat created by the Nvidia CUDA software platform. Some analysts suggest that AMD is now the top AI semiconductor stock to buy following this news. Others note that Nvidia still possesses the premier AI infrastructure solution and the best overall ecosystem.

Nvidia built its dominance by seeding the CUDA platform into universities and research labs for early AI work. This created a generation of developers who wrote original AI code optimized specifically for Nvidia chips. The company later expanded this ecosystem with CUDA-X to help scale high-performance computing workloads. Recently, Nvidia suffered reputational damage because its former CEO was linked to an alleged Chinese spy.

AMD will now roll out its new Helios system to compete for a larger market share. Nvidia still holds a lead by locking up supply-constrained high-bandwidth memory needed for chip performance. The articles leave open whether Nvidia will be forced to lower its prices to remain competitive. It remains unclear if AMD can overcome the performance lead of the Vera Rubin platform.

stories.Headline: Hyundai Home Shopping launches AI-REAL to produce full broadcasts without hosts or camera crews
stories.Summary:
Hyundai Home Shopping of South Korea is introducing a broadcast production system called AI-REAL, in which AI generates both voice and video without show hosts or camera crews. The company announced the system on November 15, 2026, for its data home shopping channel, Hyundai Home Shopping Plus Shop. The first regular application will be a November 16 broadcast at 3:20 p.m. selling Jeju Heart Gold Kiwi. Hyundai Home Shopping says this is the industry's first fully AI-produced broadcast from start to finish.

The company said it will introduce AI-REAL on its data home shopping channel, also called Hyundai Home Shopping PLUS#. AI-REAL generates on its own the voice and video needed for a broadcast, without a presenter or camera crew. The system reproduces as video everything from the cultivation environment and soil conditions of agricultural products to their distribution channels. In a pilot broadcast, partner company costs for preparing product samples and producing broadcast video fell more than 80% compared with before. Sales in the pilot reached 120% of the initial target.

Hyundai Home Shopping plans to schedule AI broadcasts at least once a month, starting with agricultural, livestock and fishery products, and later expand to processed foods and household goods. Lim Hyun-tae, head of Hyundai Home Shopping's Channel Strategy Division, said the company developed the AI broadcast system to achieve shared growth with small and mid-sized partners and to differentiate the customer shopping experience. He said the company will continue to apply AI technology to a variety of tasks to accelerate AI transformation. Lim Soo-jin, head of broadcast production at Hyundai Home Shopping, said viewers told the company the broadcast felt as natural as one with a human host. She said viewers said information such as growing conditions and cooking examples helped them decide whether to buy.

A company official said viewers responded that the AI-produced broadcast felt as natural as one hosted by an actual show host. Lotte Home Shopping is running fashion broadcasts featuring the virtual human Lucy. GS Shop has introduced an AI Studio that creates virtual broadcast spaces with generative AI and, as of September this year, had applied it to 62% of all its broadcasts. CJ OnStyle is using its AI chatbot AiON to respond in real time to customer inquiries during mobile live broadcasts.

Small and mid-sized partners will be able to introduce products without expensive production infrastructure. A reduction in the roles of broadcast production staff and show hosts is expected to be unavoidable, so changes in the industry's workforce management are also drawing attention. Previously, introducing a producing region or the production process required dedicated filming and editing staff. Until now, home shopping broadcasts were structured so that a show host's presenting ability and the quality of on-location filming determined sales performance.

The company explained that while there have been cases in the industry of using AI show hosts or producing only some video with AI, this is the first time an entire broadcast has been realized with AI. Previous uses of AI in home shopping replaced individual scenes or presenters, the company said. This case is seen as a signal that production methods in the home shopping industry are shifting from labor-centric to system-centric. Hyundai Home Shopping plans to air at least one AI-generated program a month, starting with produce, meat and seafood.

It plans to expand gradually into categories such as processed foods and household goods, where smaller suppliers have shown strong interest in selling through the retailer. Lim Hyun-tae said Hyundai Home Shopping plans to expand the use of AI across its operations. The company says it will continue to apply AI technology to a variety of tasks. The articles do not say when the expansion to processed foods and household goods will begin.

stories.Headline: Moody's chief economist Mark Zandi warns AI boom raises inflation and borrowing costs while diverting investment
stories.Summary:
Moody's Analytics Chief Economist Mark Zandi warned on Sunday in a post on X that the artificial intelligence boom is driving up inflation and borrowing costs while pulling investment away from the rest of the U.S. economy. Zandi wrote that AI has been a boon to economic growth and job creation, but he said its rapid expansion is bringing significant economic side effects. He said AI is adding to inflation by driving up electricity and consumer electronics prices, and he said AI investment is pushing up interest rates by soaking up capital to finance the AI build-out. He cautioned that the massive flow of money into AI infrastructure is coming at the expense of other investment.

Zandi said that since ChatGPT debuted four years ago, AI has gone from a rounding error to accounting for nearly two-thirds of the growth in investment. He added that growth in everything else has slowed by more than half since mid-2024. He concluded with a warning about the economic returns expected from the technology, saying the bet on AI had better pay off in higher productivity because the rest of the economy is not investing enough to deliver it. In September, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said AI infrastructure spending could reach $1 trillion in 2027, adding about 1% to GDP growth annually while potentially contributing to inflation, and he cautioned that it was too early to identify winners and losers in the AI boom.

In July, the International Monetary Fund warned that weaker-than-expected AI productivity gains could trigger a pullback in technology investment and a sharp correction in highly valued tech stocks, while raising its 2026 global inflation forecast to 4.7%. Last month, economist Peter Schiff warned that rising borrowing costs could weaken AI investment and expose broader economic vulnerabilities, while potentially benefiting gold and gold-mining stocks during an impending recession. Former Federal Reserve adviser Danielle DiMartino Booth also suggested a recession may already be underway. Al Jazeera reported that Americans are pushing back against the rapid expansion of data centers powering artificial intelligence, raising concerns over noise, pollution and energy demands.

The Benzinga article carried a disclaimer stating that its content was partially produced with the help of AI tools and was reviewed and published by Benzinga editors. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the warnings and forecasts described above.

stories.Headline: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva warns the global economy depends too heavily on AI
stories.Summary:
International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Monday, November 16, 2026, that the global economy is overly dependent on artificial intelligence. Speaking with CNBC during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in the Philippines, she cautioned that the world is standing on one leg. She explained that any instability in the AI sector could lead to significant financial stability troubles. This warning follows a recent sell-off in AI stocks and a loss of over $1 trillion in market value for Nvidia Corp.

The IMF estimates that circular financing among AI companies has grown to just over $1 trillion, with debt funding about two-thirds of that amount. This system involves investment money flowing back to investors through purchase orders, a process where Nvidia Corp plays a central role. UBS analyst Tim Arcuri noted that a pullback in Nvidia financing could remove $50 billion or more from the system. These risks emerge as the IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1 percent in October.

Kristalina Georgieva stated that investor frenzy reflects expectations that have run ahead of what the technology has actually delivered. She suggested that some market corrections are necessary because people tend to rush ahead as valuations climb. While she described recent market swings as orderly, she urged everyone to remain watchful to avoid a disorderly correction. The IMF previously warned that failing expectations could drop U.S. equity prices by 20 percent in 2026.

The AI build-out has been a critical engine for growth, especially as an energy crunch from the Iran war curtailed other sectors. Capital Economics suggested that AI-related goods accounted for as much as 80 percent of the recent expansion in global exports. The IMF also estimated that approximately 40 percent of the global workforce will be affected by AI. Investors are now awaiting earnings from Nvidia and the listing of Anthropic to see if the AI trade remains viable.

stories.Headline: Higgsfield releases AI Ad Generator for small businesses to create video adverts without studios
stories.Summary:
Higgsfield released an AI Ad Generator to help small businesses create video adverts without using a professional studio. This software allows owners in Harare, Bulawayo, and Mutare to produce content for social media. The tool turns product links or photos into finished videos without a filming crew. It targets firms selling clothes, hair products, hardware, school supplies, and various services. This shift moves production from traditional studios directly into a web browser.

The tool requires only a browser and a product description, not a server or special hardware. Users can upload five images or a link to extract names and descriptions. It offers over 40 avatars and nine modes, including UGC, Tutorial, Product Review, and Unboxing. Other modes are TV Spot, Hyper Motion, Wild Card, and two Virtual Try On options. Seedance 2.0 provides native audio and lip sync for 9:16, 16:9, and 1:1 shapes.

Higgsfield claims the process takes about two minutes from a product link to a final video. The company states the tool writes scripts, directs shots, and delivers the final cut. It says avatars can speak multiple languages, though English is the default setting. The provider notes that no design or editing experience is needed to use the suite. They suggest the tool acts as a drafting partner rather than an autopilot.

Small business owners are affected because traditional production is often too expensive or time consuming. These owners often lack the skills to write scripts, set up lighting, or edit video. Some diaspora entrepreneurs use the tool to reach customers both at home and abroad. Local users must ensure that generated scenes and accents sound credible to their audiences. They are warned not to present digital avatars as real customers giving reviews.

Interest grew after Zimbabwe launched its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in March 2026. The government urged the private sector to invest in technology and partner with start ups. Officials planned to offer incentives to businesses that integrate AI into their operations. Many firms previously relied on single photos because they lacked cameras, presenters, and quiet locations. This background makes marketing a practical starting point where the cost of mistakes is low.

Users should next test several modes for one product to see which fits their customers. They must check that prices, features, and offers shown in the adverts are true. Businesses should track views, replies, and sales to measure the success of the clips. The articles leave the specific supported languages and the current pricing plans open. Users must review the terms on commercial use before starting any paid advertising campaigns.

stories.Headline: Huawei Horinger data center has 7 percent of the compute of SpaceX Colossus 2
stories.Summary:
Ben Cottier and Lynette Bye analyzed Huawei's Horinger data center using satellite imagery on November 12, 2026. They found that this Chinese facility lags far behind the American Colossus 2. The researchers determined that Horinger has only seven percent of the compute of Colossus 2. This gap is expected to persist until at least 2028. Huawei is the biggest AI chip developer in China.

The Horinger campus in Inner Mongolia has three zones called West, South, and North. It requires up to 286 megawatts of IT power capacity across four buildings. The facility uses 105,000 Ascend 910C chips and 8,000 Ascend 910B chips. Colossus 2 is located in Tennessee and is the largest AI data center. The Horinger site demolished villages to make room for these buildings.

Epoch AI researchers are responsible for these findings and the cooling equipment model. They said that heat rejection capacity reveals the buildings' IT power capacity. The authors noted that moving fans create colored ghosts in satellite images. They stated that Horinger is likely one of the largest centers in China. They explained that US facilities extract 2.5 times more compute per unit of power.

The report affects China's AI capabilities and deployment capacity compared to the United States. Other Chinese centers like Huawei Wuhu and VNET Bayin Ulanqab may match Horinger. The analysis suggests that China's compute constraints will not ease for two years. A model like GPT-6 Astra would take one year to train at Horinger. This is possible if all current compute was combined for one run.

Huawei uses abundant energy in China to build these large AI data centers. US export controls cause Huawei to lag behind Nvidia in performance and efficiency. Nvidia's B200 and B300 chips perform at about 2.5 H100-equivalents each. Huawei's 910C chip performs at around 0.76 H100-equivalents. By March 2026, Huawei had sold 907,000 Ascend 910C and 600,000 Ascend 910B chips.

One building in the West zone should become operational by December 2026. A new building in the South zone may be operational by February 2028. This growth could increase Horinger's total AI compute by over 70 percent. Colossus 2 is expected to reach 1.8 million H100-equivalents by 2028. The articles leave open whether other Chinese data centers will fall further behind.

stories.Headline: Samsung and SK Hynix gain bargaining power as Nvidia faces leadership turmoil
stories.Summary:
Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang on November 9, 2026, causing the company's shares to fall by 4.3 percent. This leadership vacuum has shaken the AI semiconductor supply chain while creating new opportunities for South Korean memory suppliers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Anonymous employees launched a website called Stand With Jensen to petition for the return of the former chief executive officer. This petition gathered roughly 110,000 signatures, including 60,000 shareholders and 5,000 employees, to demand that Huang be reinstated and treated fairly. Silicon Valley figures like Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, and Garry Tan also joined the signature drive to support the former leader.

The situation involves high-bandwidth memory, known as HBM, and requires a diversified customer base to increase the bargaining power of the memory suppliers. Samsung Electronics signed a priority HBM4 supply deal with AMD in March and partnered with Anthropic to manufacture its own AI chips. SK Hynix holds a near-monopoly on memory supply for Google's in-house Tensor Processing Unit chips, which Google has begun selling externally. Other companies deploying self-developed chips in data centers include Amazon with Trainium and Microsoft with the Maia 100 chip. US lawmakers are now pressing for tighter controls on AI chip exports to China following the allegations involving Jensen Huang.

Erwin Cummins, a senior research staff engineer at Nvidia, stated that Huang's leadership was the driving force that brought employees to the company. Lee Ji-hwan, CEO of Aurora Investment Advisory, said memory demand is not significantly affected whether Nvidia wobbles or rivals like AMD and Google replace it. Kim Young-gun of Mirae Asset Securities diagnosed that Samsung and SK Hynix can strengthen bargaining power through the diversification of their customers. Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker said on X that facts must be verified and an investigation must determine if Huang serves shareholders. These experts believe that the shift from AI training to the inference phase will continue to underpin the demand for memory.

Dylan Patel, CEO of SemiAnalysis, said that Google and others might take significant market share because Huang is the only executive who can secure production. Major customers of Nvidia are reducing their dependence by developing application-specific integrated circuits, which is a trend that benefits the memory industry. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are affected by these shifts, as well as by the potential for tighter US export curbs to China. A fake letter impersonating Vice President Ian Buck and Chief Scientist Bill Dally circulated on X, demanding the resignation of the entire board. This fraudulent document was a modified version of the open letter from when OpenAI CEO Sam Altman was ousted in 2023.

The background shows that SK Hynix had about a quarter of its revenue coming from Nvidia during the previous year of business operations. The memory industry views the current reshuffle as an opportunity because more diversified chip design companies create a more stable demand base. The rise of competitors like AMD and Google is reshaping the supply chain as they target gaps in the market built by Nvidia. AI infrastructure investment is not expected to shrink, but the center of gravity is moving from the training phase to the inference phase. The trend of rising HBM content in advanced application-specific integrated circuits provides a tailwind for the South Korean memory companies.

Next, investors must watch trading volume and foreign flows to see if Samsung Electronics can enter a full-fledged uptrend in its share price. Market observers believe that the negotiating power of memory companies will rise further if the structure of diversified chip design takes hold. The industry must determine if the market can absorb the selling volume from investors who bought Samsung shares at past high prices. The articles leave open whether the independent investigation into Jensen Huang will result in his permanent removal or his eventual reinstatement. It remains uncertain how the push for tighter China chip curbs will specifically impact the future revenues of Samsung and SK Hynix.

stories.Headline: Dublin City Council pilots AI flood warning system with EMR Integrated Solutions
stories.Summary:
Dublin City Council will pilot a new artificial intelligence early warning system for major flood events in Dublin City, the Irish Examiner reported on Monday, 16 November, 2026. The project is run in partnership with critical infrastructure specialist EMR Integrated Solutions, which gathered the sensor data used by the model. The pilot is set to run through this autumn and winter, according to the Irish Examiner. Silicon Republic reported that the rollout covers the autumn and winter of late 2026 and early 2027. Trials of the technology using historical events showed potential early warnings of 13 to 21 hours for some mountain rain-driven events.

The AI model draws on ten years' worth of sensor data gathered by EMR Integrated Solutions, including river level readings, rainfall measurements, tide data and data from Met Éireann. The project could warn between 13 and 21 hours ahead of events, which Dublin City Council says will give staff and response teams more time to prepare and act. EMR has operated Dublin City Council's regional flood monitoring system for nine years through outstations in the city and surrounding counties that monitor rainfall, river levels, tide readings and more. EMR was founded in the 1980s and is based in Dunboyne, Co Meath, and works with sectors including water, power, utilities, corporate business, broadcasting and public safety organisations. EMR has an agreement with Dublin City Council to provide engineers to support the council's flood management through associated site work, installations, repairs and instrument calibration.

Minister for Climate, Environment and Energy Darragh O'Brien, TD, welcomed the initiative and said the single most valuable thing we can give people is time. O'Brien said the pilot shows how AI can turn the data we already have into earlier, clearer warnings, helping engineers and emergency services make better decisions when it matters most. He said he very much welcomed the initiative from EMR Integrated Solutions and Dublin City Council and looked forward to seeing the results. Dublin City Council chief executive Richard Shakespeare said the pilot is likely to demonstrate how technology and data can be harnessed to support better decision-making and improve preparedness for flooding events. Shakespeare said the council is committed to further embracing appropriate AI technology that helps protect communities, homes and critical infrastructure as climate change increases the frequency and intensity of severe weather events.

EMR chief commercial officer Mark O'Connor said we know we can't stop the rain, nor can we prevent every flood, but we can potentially give people something they cannot buy, time to prepare and prevent, and time for the council to take action. Dennis Keeley, Dublin City Council's assistant chief executive for climate and urban resilience, said one of the greatest challenges during flooding events is ensuring operational teams have sufficient time to deploy resources, protect critical infrastructure and respond effectively to emerging risks. Keeley said the AI technology could help reduce disruption to communities, minimise damage to public assets and enhance public safety during extreme weather events. According to EMR, a central principle for the pilot system is that all decisions remain with qualified Dublin City Council staff, who can review and interpret alerts generated by the AI model based on its analysis of signals and patterns in the relevant data. EMR said the project aims to allow timely delivery of accurate and relevant information to residents who may be affected, supporting greater awareness, preparedness and community resilience.

Shakespeare said the pilot aligns strongly with the ambitions set out in the Dublin City Council Corporate Plan, particularly the commitment to building a climate-resilient city and delivering high-quality public services through innovation and collaboration. He referred to recent engagements with telemetry and SCADA provider EMR Integrated Solutions. O'Brien said we have seen in the past the devastating effect flooding has on homes, businesses and communities around Dublin. The Irish Examiner reported that trials of the tech show it can give between 13 and 21 hours of early warnings for some mountain rain-driven events. The AI model will rapidly analyse the data sets provided to staff and then give a more reliable warning of conditions which could lead to serious flooding.

The pilot is set to run through this autumn and winter, and Silicon Republic reported the rollout covers the autumn and winter of late 2026 and early 2027. O'Brien said he looked forward to seeing the results of the initiative from EMR Integrated Solutions and Dublin City Council. Shakespeare said the pilot is likely to demonstrate how technology and data can be harnessed to support better decision-making and improve preparedness for flooding events. According to EMR, all decisions remain with qualified Dublin City Council staff, who can review and interpret alerts generated by the AI model. The articles do not state what will happen after the pilot ends or whether the system will be made permanent.

stories.Headline: Shenzhen launches AI action plan to boost technological cooperation with Asia-Pacific partners
stories.Summary:
Shenzhen is preparing to host the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting from November 18 to 19, 2026, under a theme of shared prosperity. This event highlights the potential for deeper artificial intelligence cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region, including the use of humanoid robots for agricultural tasks. Local firms like EngineAI Robotics Technology Co., Ltd. are testing robot movement to eventually help Malaysian farmers harvest oil palm fruit and pollinate durian trees. These efforts demonstrate how Chinese innovation can move beyond exporting products to developing new applications with local partners.

The city's core AI industry generated approximately 220 billion yuan in revenue during 2025, supported by over 2,600 large enterprises. Trade between Shenzhen and other APEC economies reached 1.98 trillion yuan in the first half of 2026, representing nearly 70 percent of the city's foreign trade. To support this growth, Shenzhen released an AI action plan for 2026 to 2028 in September, focusing on cooperation with ASEAN and Belt and Road Initiative countries. Additionally, China plans to provide 5,000 AI training opportunities for developing countries over five years and will establish a cross-border data flow center in Qianhai.

Various leaders and experts believe that these technological advancements can drive regional digital transformation and economic growth. Yao Qiyuan of EngineAI Robotics noted that expanding overseas involves creating new applications with partners rather than just selling goods. Hu Zhenyu from the China Development Institute stated that the city is now exporting entire industrial chains to meet demand in Latin America and Southeast Asia. Eduardo Pedrosa, the APEC Secretariat Executive Director, explained that the leaders' meeting is in Shenzhen because the city's research and innovation can benefit the entire world.

This cooperation aligns with the APEC Artificial Intelligence Initiative for 2026 to 2030, which was adopted in 2025 to foster resilient economic growth. The 2026 Chengdu Statement, adopted on July 23, further encourages member economies to support small businesses with affordable digital solutions. Because micro, small and medium-sized enterprises make up over 97 percent of regional businesses, AI is seen as a way to lower technology barriers. Future efforts will likely focus on promoting secure AI ecosystems and enhancing industrial collaboration across the 21 member economies.

stories.Headline: Downing Street aide reads ChatGPT feedback on Burnham speech draft on train
stories.Summary:
An unnamed Downing Street speechwriter was photographed on Friday reading ChatGPT’s suggestions for making the prime minister’s speech more emotive, according to the Mail on Sunday. The aide to Andy Burnham was seen on the 5.03pm train from London Euston to Holyhead as Burnham and his team headed to the Welsh Labour conference with a bottle of bubbly. The pictures were taken while the aide sipped prosecco and read the AI chatbot’s feedback on a passage criticising the legacy of Margaret Thatcher. An image of the aide’s phone screen showed ChatGPT commenting on lines about Thatcher’s impact on working men’s clubs, choirs and other social infrastructure in the 1980s. Burnham later delivered the speech at the Welsh Labour Conference in Llandudno, in northern Wales, and did not use the specific passage seen in the pictures.

The chatbot said it preferred the second passage because it moves from the miners to their families to the wider community, showing how industrial work created bonds beyond the workplace. In the speech, Burnham said Thatcher shattered the way of life for communities up and down Britain with mines closed, factories closed and steelworks silenced. He also said cost of living is the top issue in Wales, as it is in all parts of the UK. Burnham spoke of the workplaces that created a way of life, the social infrastructure taken for granted, the working men’s clubs, the sports teams, the choirs and the trade unions, adding that people came together and looked out for each other. Elsewhere he said Labour had lost power in Wales after elections earlier this year, that the party may have lost sight of the principles that drove devolution, and that for the first time in its history Labour is not leading the Welsh Government.

A No 10 spokesperson said the PM writes most of his own speeches and that an aide sought feedback on a speech draft that had already been written. The Express reported the spokesperson saying the PM writes most of his own speeches and this one was no exception. Reform UK chairman Lee Anderson told the Mail on Sunday that it must be thirsty work writing speeches for Burnham. Anderson said his bubbly-drinking socialists have no plan to tackle the cost-of-living crisis and that AI Andy’s man-of-the-people act has been exposed as a sham. He added that Burnham is an artificial prime minister who does not have the faintest clue what he believes or what he is doing.

The use of ChatGPT and other AI chatbots by politicians and their aides has drawn plenty of attention since the tech first emerged earlier this decade. Addressing the House of Commons last year, Conservative MP Tom Tugendhat blasted colleagues for supposedly using AI to write their own speeches, saying the phrase I rise to speak is a giveaway. Tugendhat said all they were hearing was the ChatGPT generated press releases. He said ChatGPT knows you’re there, but that is an Americanism we don’t use, and told colleagues to keep using it because it makes clear the place has become absurd. The Express reported that the AI tool suggested using an emotive passage describing working men’s clubs, choirs and other social infrastructure lost as Britain moved away from its industrial base.

The photographs were taken on Friday as Burnham and his team travelled to the Welsh Labour conference, and the speech was delivered on Saturday. The Mail on Sunday published the pictures of the aide’s phone screen showing ChatGPT’s feedback on the Thatcher passage. The articles do not say whether the aide faced any disciplinary action or whether Downing Street investigated the matter further. They do not name the speechwriter or say how the photographs were obtained. They also do not say whether Burnham commented on the photographs himself.

stories.Headline: EU leaders postpone AI discussions to focus on Ukraine negotiations at Dublin summit
stories.Summary:
EU leaders gathered in Dublin on November 13 and 14 for a summit focused on artificial intelligence and regional security. The meetings were derailed when the Ukraine issue became the main focus after US envoys met with President Zelensky. European leaders shifted their attention to forming a negotiating team to speak with one voice to the outside world. The ninth European Political Community summit occurred Thursday, followed by an informal European Union leaders meeting on Friday. These high-level gatherings took place at the Convention Centre Dublin, which overlooks the River Liffey in Ireland.

The summit required a negotiating team consisting of EU institutions and five Coalition of the Willing countries, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland. Ursula von der Leyen proposed spending 30 billion euros, or 33.07 billion US dollars, to build seven AI gigafactories. She estimated that Europe actually needs at least 500 billion euros, or 551.10 billion dollars, to advance its broader technological ambitions. The 2023 Chips Act aimed for 20 percent of the global market, but the industry now declares this goal unattainable. Ireland held the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU during the second half of 2026.

European Council President Antonio Costa announced the formation of the negotiating team and said leaders would revisit AI in February 2027. Ursula von der Leyen outlined the gigafactory plans, while President Emmanuel Macron called for faster decisions and much greater investment. Macron and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten will convene a meeting of European technology leaders in Paris on December 2. President Zelensky described recent talks in Abu Dhabi as serious and urged Europe to secure a regular place in negotiations. These leaders sought a greater say in decisions affecting the future of Europe and the security of the region.

Around 1,000 pro-Palestinian demonstrators marched toward the National Gallery of Ireland to protest military spending and the neutrality of Ireland. More than 5,000 Irish police officers managed security, causing road closures and transport restrictions that disrupted daily life in Dublin. The Irish Times noted that these security operations caused public disruption and raised questions about the costs of hosting gatherings. The Centre for European Policy Studies warned that relying on foreign chip suppliers could create new and dangerous technological dependencies. The Financial Times reported that productivity gains from AI in Europe have remained modest despite some new industrial activity.

The 2000 Lisbon Strategy aimed to build a competitive knowledge economy by 2010, but it failed and became the Europe 2020 Strategy. This second strategy also failed because subsidizing farmers and saving factories wins more votes than spending on long-term competitiveness. Europe now faces funding gaps for Ukraine and a 22nd round of sanctions, with more financial discussions coming soon. The region struggles with strategic anxiety and a lack of hard power in computing, chips, and advanced AI models. This pattern shows a tendency to retreat to coordination rather than committing real money to achieve clear strategic objectives.

EU leaders will return to discuss Ukraine financing needs at their next meeting on November 26 and 27. Territorial disputes and security guarantees for Ukraine remain unresolved, and the appointment of a single European envoy is still open. The future of the AI gigafactory plan remains stalled and tied to negotiations over the next long-term EU budget. The articles leave open whether Europe can maintain strategic autonomy without depending on any third party for its international role. It remains unclear if the 27 member states will agree to pay the funds needed for technological competitiveness.

stories.Headline: GIGABYTE launches AI TOP AERO personal studio for local AI development and content creation
stories.Summary:
GIGABYTE announced the launch of the AI TOP AERO personal AI studio on November 16, 2026, in the city of Taipei. This new desktop computer is powered by the NVIDIA RTX Spark platform to expand the local AI solutions offered by GIGABYTE. The system is designed to bring local AI development, gaming, and content creation directly into personal workspaces for various professional users. It allows users to run larger AI models locally on their own devices without needing to depend on cloud computing services. This product combines a GPU with NVIDIA Blackwell architecture and a compact chassis design to create a powerful and thin PC.

The AI TOP AERO uses the NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X Superchip, which integrates a 20 core NVIDIA Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU. It runs on Windows 11 and offers up to 128 GB of LPDDR5x unified memory and a 4 TB PCIe Gen5 SSD. The compact chassis measures approximately one liter and includes USB Type-C, 10 GbE Ethernet, and Wi-Fi 7 for connecting various external peripherals. It supports NVIDIA DLSS 5 for gaming and uses NVIDIA PAIR to distribute inference tasks across a local network of available devices. The system is built to handle professional workloads and AI inference through a specialized GIGABYTE cooling design for thermal headroom.

GIGABYTE is responsible for the hardware integration and the cooling design that maintains performance during long periods of high professional workloads. The company stated that the AI TOP AERO responds to needs for data privacy, faster response times, and lower usage costs. They explained that the device integrates AI technology into the daily tools, personal data, and existing workflows of the target users. GIGABYTE noted that their hardware experience allows this compact format to provide the necessary performance for prolonged and demanding computing use. The company claims the system provides a fluid experience by integrating various applications, tools, and workflows into one single personal studio.

The product is specifically targeted at developers, creators, and AI users who want to process data and test applications on their devices. Developers can use the NVIDIA CUDA platform to create, prototype, tune, and run the latest open models locally on the system. These users can employ NVIDIA Nemotron compatible models and CUDA accelerated tools to explore local inference and agentic AI application testing. Content creators can use ComfyUI for generative AI workflows, while NVIDIA Broadcast and RTX Video improve the quality of audio and video. Gamers are affected by the inclusion of neural rendering, which provides more detailed lighting and materials in supported games via DLSS 5.

The articles state that generative AI is moving beyond conversational assistants toward AI agents, content generation, and the automation of various workflows. Users are seeking more personal AI computing options to maintain privacy and control over their data while avoiding the costs of cloud. GIGABYTE previously expanded its local AI development options by making the 64 GB unified memory version of the AI TOP ATOM available. The company also received a CES 2027 Innovation Award for its AORUS C510 GLASS INFINITY tower, showing its ongoing focus on hardware. This new studio is an extension of the current range of AI solutions that GIGABYTE provides for the global market.

The AI TOP AERO was scheduled for official release on November 10, 2026, to provide a new option for local AI development. Users can utilize additional compatible tools such as Ollama and LM Studio to create a local AI environment tailored to individual needs. The system allows for continuous agents to be available 24 hours a day while keeping all inference and data on device. The articles leave the specific pricing and the exact availability in different regions open for users to check via local communications. They do not specify the exact cost of the different memory configurations or the specific retail partners for the product.

stories.Headline: Stanford researchers open source Memorilla to provide latent semantic memory for frozen LLMs
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Stanford University developed Memorilla, a latent semantic memory system for large language models, which was released in November 2026. This open source system condenses entire document collections into a fixed number of query dependent memory tokens for frozen models. It allows these frozen models to process extensive data with improved accuracy and efficiency while significantly reducing total token usage. The system reads a whole document collection and provides the model with just 16 memory tokens for each question. This approach achieves better average performance than other methods such as Mem0 and MemoRAG, according to the research team.

The system requires Linux with CUDA GPUs and Python 3.11, using NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs for its training recipes. It utilizes a 194M parameter trainable memory module with a frozen Qwen3-Embedding-4B encoder and a frozen Qwen3-8B decoder. Training takes 19 hours on four H100 GPUs, downloading 310 GiB of data and embeddings across three distinct stages. The first stage uses 1.98M Wikipedia examples, the second adds 1.34M QA examples, and the third fine tunes on benchmarks. Checkpoints are available on Hugging Face at memorilla/Memorilla-Qwen3-8B under the Apache 2.0 license for public use and deployment.

The work comes from Jure Leskovec's SNAP group, with co authors from MIT, Penn, and the University of Toronto. The researchers stated that Memorilla learns what each question needs from the whole store rather than using retrieval chunks. They reported that the system achieves 84.33 per cent accuracy on FactKG, which is higher than the 80.43 per cent full context. The team noted that the memory module can scale to millions of tokens while consistently using only 16 memory tokens. They also claimed the highest reported average across eight benchmarks, with a score of 49.68 for the system.

The system affects frozen LLMs by removing the need for full context prompting, which slows down as history grows. It outperforms xRAG on PersonaMem-v2 with 44.60 per cent accuracy, compared to 30.90 per cent for the next best method. However, it performs worse on PubMedQA, scoring 59.00 per cent against 69.00 per cent for LLMLingua-2 due to small abstract sizes. MemoRAG leads on NarrativeQA ROUGE-L with 20.51 versus 19.31 and on PersonalizationV4 with 67.88 per cent versus 66.65 per cent. The system also helps agents, raising the average success rate on TextWorld games from 18.6 per cent to 24.2 per cent.

Full context prompting is slower than Memorilla, which answers in 0.74 seconds for 512 documents versus 19.9 seconds for full context. The system can compress books and movie scripts from NarrativeQA by over 4,000 times, replacing 67,385 tokens with 16 tokens. A memory cache can reduce processing for one million documents to 8.1 milliseconds, or 5.0 milliseconds using torch.compile. This cache costs 80 GiB at four million documents, where a question takes 33 milliseconds to process on one B200. The research team also released PersonalizationV4, featuring 149 synthetic users with 200 conversations each under a CC BY 4.0 license.

Users can install the system with uv on Linux and load the model using the MemoryVLLM.from_pretrained function for deployment. The first run requires downloading about 25 GB of models, and custom data needs parquet files with specific column names. Each checkpoint must run with the specific decoder it was trained with to ensure the evaluation documents remain accurate. The articles leave open whether any quantized variants of the memory module will be disclosed for users with smaller GPUs. They do not state if the system will be expanded to support decoders other than the Qwen3 series.

stories.Headline: Google agrees to pay $10 million for Spirit Airlines corporate data
stories.Summary:
Google agreed to pay $10 million for bankrupt Spirit Airlines’ corporate data, covering some 31 years of internal workflows, Cedar News reported on 2026-11-15. Cedar News said a new market is taking shape around one of businesses’ most overlooked assets, their internal data. The Cedar News item appeared under the headline that frontier labs are buying up internal company data to train AI. Cedar News said the marketplace is booming, despite privacy concerns. The potential payouts are substantial, Cedar News said.

Bain & Company estimated spending of up to US$6.5tn to build nearly 150GW of new compute capacity by 2030. Bain expected 20, 30% growth in data centre critical capacity over the next five years. Hyperscalers’ data centre CapEx could top US$1tn by 2028, Bain said. The number of semiconductor companies manufacturing the most advanced logic node fell 84%, from 25 companies in 2002, 2003 to 4 companies from 2020-2026. Global data centre electricity demand is estimated to more than double from an estimated 589TWh in 2026 to 1,228TWh in 2030, and North America’s virtual power plant market is 37.5GW.

Adam Mayer, Technical Product Marketing Director at Qlik, wrote in TechRadar on 13 November 2026 that data privacy is becoming harder to manage as businesses give AI applications and agents access to more internal systems. Mayer said much of the focus has been on the risk of AI models surfacing sensitive or confidential information in their responses, but the privacy challenge starts earlier. He said organizations also need to understand what data AI systems can access in the first place, where that data comes from and how it is being used. Mayer said 95% of enterprises have delayed or cancelled AI projects because of infrastructure and data governance challenges. He said businesses need to get the foundations right before privacy risks become impossible to contain.

Mayer said data privacy is not just a legal or compliance concern and should matter to everyone who touches data within an organization. He said the consequences of getting it wrong are growing, from exposing sensitive information to damaging customer trust and brand reputation. Mayer said poorly classified, duplicated or outdated data can carry existing privacy problems into AI applications, turning weaknesses previously contained within individual systems into much wider risks. He said agentic AI raises the stakes further because agents can increasingly surface and act on information across multiple parts of the business. Mayer said personally identifiable information such as names, addresses or financial details should be clearly labelled so it can be spotted before it is moved.

Mayer said identifying sensitive data is only the first step in managing the privacy challenge. He said businesses also need to track where it moves, particularly when information is copied from live systems into testing or development environments which may not have the same security controls in place. He said sensitive information should remain within the live systems where it is needed wherever possible. Mayer said removing or masking identifying details can reduce the risk of unnecessary exposure if data does need to be used elsewhere. Bain said building AI-ready data centres is proving as much a test of supply chains and power infrastructure as it is of capital.

Bain’s figures were drawn from the December Week 1 edition of Data Centre Magazine, which sets out the scale of the challenge from the spending required to deliver nearly 150GW of new compute capacity by 2030 to the shrinking number of manufacturers able to produce the most advanced chips. Bain’s figures also point to sharply rising electricity demand and a growing virtual power plant market in North America. Cedar News said the potential payouts are substantial, evidenced by Google’s agreement to pay $10 million for Spirit Airlines’ corporate data. TechRadar published Mayer’s opinion piece on 13 November 2026 under the title that AI privacy starts with your data. Data Centre Magazine published its Bain statistics article on November 15, 2026.

stories.Headline: Armin Ashenberg argues universities must teach graduates to collaborate with AI as automation reshapes the job market
stories.Summary:
Dr Armin D Ashenberg of the School of Law at Western Sydney University wrote an opinion piece first published with full links on The Conversation. The piece was also published by Western Sydney University on 16 November 2026. It addresses concerns about artificial intelligence taking people's jobs and reducing job opportunities for university graduates. AI software companies such as OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic are pursuing AI systems capable of matching or exceeding human performance across a broad range of intellectual tasks. The article asks what this means for graduates and universities and which jobs are most at risk.

A federal government report published in July rated jobs typically involving cognitive tasks as those with the highest exposure to AI automation, including accountants, clerks and receptionists. Jobs rated as lowest exposure tended to require more physical work, such as tradies, carers and truck drivers. The report found that as of February this year AI had not had significant impacts on the Australian job market, including graduate opportunities. This month the Reserve Bank of Australia noted some signs younger workers in more AI-exposed industries are struggling to find work in Australia. The number of graduate jobs in some law firms has been slashed, with low-level tasks passed onto AI, and consulting firms have also cut graduate roles in recent years but claim it is not because of AI.

Just last week Qantas announced it will outsource 850 jobs to India while investing more in AI. A 2024 study compared the reasoning skills of humans and AI language models through tests including maths puzzles designed to assess whether people and AI models could recognise that an answer, which seems right at first, is actually wrong. In the example given, a scarf costs 210€ more than a hat, the scarf and the hat cost 220€ in total, and the correct answer for the hat is 5€. Researchers found earlier AI systems performed worse than human participants in the study's reasoning test, while more recent AI models performed better. An OpenAI model recently disproved a longstanding conjecture in geometry dating back to 1946.

Ashenberg's own research analysed AI's responses on university criminal law exams in 2023 and 2025, finding average exam scores improved from 52.5% in 2023 to 76.3% in 2025. Unlike the 2023 study, the 2025 models on average performed better than an average university student on critical thinking capabilities. These were specific tests and do not prove AI could displace humans and take over an entire profession, but the results challenge the assumption AI weaknesses will remain unchanged. Robotaxis carry passengers in a growing number of cities, delivery robots bring meals to customers and autonomous excavators dig on construction sites. In a 2026 pilot study health-care professionals, mostly nurses, accepted half the deliberately wrong AI recommendations and passed over about one in six correct ones.

In a study looking at how the UK public uses AI for medical advice, researchers found people sometimes left out important details when consulting chatbots, so the chatbots sometimes mixed useful suggestions with misleading ones. The article is part of a series on how AI is reshaping higher education, taking a deeper look into how AI has disrupted degrees, how universities are responding and what the technology means for the sector's future. The article states that if a sufficiently capable AI could control reliable, affordable robots then electricians and plumbers could also face competition. It adds that despite significant progress in robots' ability to carry out complex physical tasks it is still unclear how soon they will be able to do more of the work tradies do. For now, students who choose vocational pathways such as apprenticeships may face a lower risk of AI-related job disruption.

The article argues the possibility of humans working with AI should be central to how universities prepare students for the workforce, because if a worker can't improve the quality or efficiency of AI's output an employer may have little economic reason to involve them. It says graduates may need to understand what a good result looks like when using AI, recognise when AI falls short, and have the knowledge and skills to improve AI's output. It says they also need to learn how to collaborate with AI, how to direct it, question its output and persist until the result is better than what it produced initially. It states universities can't simply replace disciplinary knowledge with AI skills, and students will need the knowledge and skills their degrees have always required as well as the ability to collaborate effectively with AI. It concludes that a technology designed to make our lives easier may actually require us to work harder to stay relevant in the job market.

stories.Headline: Japanese manufacturers report higher profits as AI demand lifts earnings
stories.Summary:
Many publicly traded Japanese companies reported higher profits for the first half of the current business year ending in March. These financial gains occurred during the period from April to September and were driven by the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. Firms within the manufacturing sector performed particularly well as they capitalized on the robust demand for new technology. Several of these organizations have already revised their full-year earnings forecasts upward to reflect this growth. The current economic shift requires these companies to adapt their production and financial planning to meet the surging demand for AI.

This trend changes the outlook for the manufacturing sector by increasing the expected revenue for the remainder of the fiscal year. Every firm that closes its books in March must now account for these unexpected gains in their official reports. The surge in profits indicates a broader transition toward integrating artificial intelligence across various industrial applications. Yoshimitsu Goto, who serves as the Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of SoftBank Group, spoke about these developments.

He addressed the current business climate during an online news conference held on Tuesday to discuss the financial landscape. While the specific details of his remarks were not fully detailed, his presence highlighted the importance of the AI boom. He represents a major player in the technology sector that is closely monitoring these market shifts. The broader context involves a period of significant growth for Japanese firms despite growing uncertainty in the global market.

These companies are leveraging the AI boom to strengthen their positions against international competitors in the tech space. Future reports will likely determine if this profit trend continues through the end of the business year. Analysts are watching to see if other sectors beyond manufacturing will experience similar financial boosts. More to follow.
