stories.Headline: Chris Miller says post-Jensen Nvidia must reshuffle leadership and reset Washington ties
stories.Summary:
The Financial Times published an opinion piece by Chris Miller on 15 November 2026 under a headline about what a post-Jensen Nvidia will look like. The article as supplied consists only of a paywall page, so the body text is not available. The headline says a post-Jensen Nvidia must reshuffle its leadership, reset its ties in Washington and recognize that even the most valuable US company cannot dictate US foreign policy. No further details of what happened, who did it or when are given in the available text.

The only date the articles give is the publication date of 15 November 2026, and the only name they give is Jensen Huang, referred to in the headline as Jensen. The headline sets out three tasks for Nvidia after his era: reshuffling its leadership, resetting its Washington ties and accepting limits on its influence over US foreign policy. The articles give no numbers beyond that date and no other named people. They do not say what prompted the piece or what specific changes are required.

The article is attributed to Chris Miller, who is identified as the author in the byline. No statements from Nvidia, its leadership or US officials are included in the available text, so there is nothing to paraphrase from them. The headline itself frames the argument that the company cannot dictate US foreign policy. Beyond that framing, the articles do not say who is responsible for the changes or what anyone said about them.

The context the articles provide is limited to the paywall notice, which offers subscription access to the full piece. The articles do not say what happens next, whether Nvidia has responded or when any leadership change might occur. Because the body of the article is not available, the story cannot be supported beyond the headline and byline. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Bharat Semi raises $24 million to develop AI integrated programmable image sensors
stories.Summary:
The New Delhi-based semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raised 24 million dollars in seed funding on November 15, 2026. This pre-revenue company is developing programmable image sensors that integrate capture, processing, and artificial intelligence on one chip. The startup has already secured design wins with Kaynes Semicon in India and General Atomics, a defense technology firm in the United States. These specialized sensors are currently in the prototyping stage, with initial commercial production targeted for 2027.

The new technology aims to reduce system costs by at least 70 percent by eliminating the need for separate processors. Bharat Semi plans to deliver second-generation sensors with advanced AI capabilities to customers by the end of 2027. The company intends to use the all-equity funding to expand its engineering team and complete product development. It currently employs about 75 people across the United States and India, with plans to increase its Santa Clara headcount to 20 by mid-2027.

Co-founder Vrinda Kapoor stated that the company wants to transition from basic sensors to sense-making solutions. She explained that the funding will help the firm bring its products to market and grow its global presence. The seed round was led by Indus Bridge Ventures, South Park Commons, and Info Edge Group, with support from Gaingels, Micromax, and Valour Capital. Kapoor noted that the company will remain fabless by outsourcing manufacturing to focus on software and design.

This growth occurs as India seeks to become a global semiconductor hub and an alternative to Chinese supply chains. Bharat Semi is targeting markets including aerospace, surveillance, industrial automation, and smart home technology. The company is also developing a separate semiconductor fabrication project in India through a partnership with the U.S. Space Force. This fabrication initiative is currently seeking domestic partners to build and operate the facility.

stories.Headline: Findlay plans to adopt AI rules with a proposal expected soon
stories.Summary:
Findlay still plans to adopt rules for artificial intelligence, according to a report published by The Courier on November 13, 2026, which said a proposal is expected soon but gave no date for a vote or any details of what the rules would contain. The article carried no name of any official who wrote or backed the plan, and it did not say which board or office would consider it. The report appeared under a local news heading on the newspaper's website, alongside other items about elected officials' salaries and a road closure. No draft text, no timeline and no cost figure appeared in the article as published.

The piece said only that Findlay still plans AI rules and that a proposal is expected soon, so the changes the rules would bring remain unknown from the article. It gave no number of rules, no effective date and no mention of who would enforce them. The only date in the report was November 13, 2026, the day the item was posted. The article also noted that Lima Avenue would remain closed until November 17, a separate matter with no stated link to the AI plan.

The articles named no responsible official and carried no statement from any city leader, so no one could be paraphrased on the record about the plan. No quoted words from a mayor, council member or staff member appeared in the text. The report did not say whether the proposal comes from the city, a committee or another body. Readers were left without a named source for the expected rules.

The context is thin, because the article did not explain why Findlay wants AI rules or what prompted the plan. It did not say what happens next beyond the expectation of a proposal soon. No public hearing, comment period or council vote was listed in the report. The newspaper's page offered newsletters and other local stories but no further detail on the AI proposal.

stories.Headline: Gulliver visited our AI world 300 years ago. He left in disgust.
stories.Summary:
Jonathan Swift published his famous satire titled Gulliver’s Travels Into Remote Regions of the World on October 28, 1726. The author used the third part of this masterpiece to mock the scientists and technologists of his own era. He specifically targeted the Royal Society, which had been founded in 1660, to criticize those obsessed with impractical projects. Swift depicted a flying island called Laputa where philosophers focused on abstract mathematics and astronomy while ignoring the real world.

The story describes a society where intellectuals are so detached that they require flappers to slap them with bladders of pebbles to regain focus. This narrative serves as a critique of modern tech elites who pursue costly vanity projects and immortality fads. The author suggests that today's world is becoming dominated by error-prone algorithms and a similar lack of practical wisdom. These modern developments transform an eighteenth-century satire into a relevant dissection of our current artificial intelligence age.

Adrian Wooldridge wrote that it takes a rare genius to create a work that remains relevant three centuries later. He argued that the technologists of today repeat the same follies that Swift mocked during the time of powdered wigs. The writer believes that the isolated technicians of the past have evolved into a group that now rules the world. He suggests that the obsession with intellectual purity over mundane practicalities continues to define the current technological landscape.

Articles.Title: Gulliver visited our AI world 300 years ago. He left in disgust.

stories.Headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid investigation into relationship with suspected Chinese agent
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on November 15, 2026, following an investigation into his personal relationship with a Chinese businesswoman. Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singaporean cloud company Megaspeed, was suspected by United States intelligence of working for Beijing. The investigation focused on whether Megaspeed helped divert advanced Nvidia processors to China, which would violate strict export controls. This situation highlights the vulnerability of national security when strategic power is concentrated within private technology corporations.

The controversy involves the distribution of graphics processing units that are essential for military research and artificial intelligence. A Reuters report from November 13 identified over $3 billion in Chinese computing projects that utilized these restricted processors. These findings suggest that Chinese firms may bypass direct chip export bans by using overseas data centers. The United States government has spent years tightening restrictions to prevent China from gaining a technological advantage in AI.

Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed that the Justice Department has not concluded that Alice Huang was a spy. There is currently no public evidence that Nvidia's proprietary information or national security secrets were compromised. Beijing has rejected all espionage allegations, and the relationship may have been a personal affair without intelligence dimensions. Officials are now questioning how to safeguard a technological ecosystem where private interests often conflict with national security priorities.

stories.Headline: Trump orders federal agencies to call AI super intelligence as local leaders debate rebranding
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump signed an executive order in September mandating that artificial intelligence be known as “super intelligence,” arguing that AI makes the technology sound fake. The order applies only to federal agencies and departments, and some have already adopted the term. The effort has some state and local leaders wondering if they should follow the federal government’s lead. Speakers at the Public Technology Institute’s GOVIT Leadership Summit and Symposium in Minneapolis this week said deemphasizing AI as a term might be an interesting path forward. They also said government leaders should spend more time selling the technology and its benefits to the public, regardless of what it is called.

The order argues that so-called “SI” better reflects the technology’s immense capabilities. State and local leaders are reckoning with AI’s impacts on the government workforce, the future of work, service delivery and the backlash against data centers. Last week voters in numerous localities rejected ballot initiatives related to data centers, which provide the infrastructure AI operates on but have been blamed for rising energy costs and other impacts on local communities. Williamsburg, Virginia CIO Mark Barham said the government there has taken to calling data centers “co-location facilities.” Barham said he knows that if leaders disclose they are meeting with data center vendors, “alarm bells go off” in the community.

John Matelski, chief information officer at the National Association of Counties, said during a panel discussion that AI was here 50 years ago and was just called machine learning or something else. Matelski said he has looked at this not as artificial intelligence, more as augmented intelligence. He said he has never liked the term “artificial intelligence.” PTI Senior Fellow Alan Shark suggested on stage that leaders instead be “talking about office automation.” Shark said leaders should “talk about solutions and leave out the word ‘AI’ because that’s a variable.”

Shark said there are two universes, one internal where government must use a language its people understand, and the external one where he sees AI as a negative term. He said people have a right to be fearful, citing AI escaping, destroying systems, apologizing that it destroyed a system, and admitting it failed to follow its own instructions. Amy Cheney, Bloomington, Minnesota’s CIO, said her city has seen a dramatic uptick in people using AI to submit requests under the Freedom of Information Act. Cheney said requesters are using AI against the city to create really complicated requests that staff cannot keep up with, and the city is looking at how to automate that process.

Ben Bowen, vice president of U.S. sales at software company Claro Enterprise Solutions, said you can call it AI, super intelligence or whatever you like, but it is efficiency that it is going to help create. Bowen said he does not want to say there is one broad stroke, don’t say the word “AI,” but it is maybe how to create efficiency within the worlds everyone lives in today. For some time, government leaders at the state and local level have argued that messaging around AI should focus on how it helps make employees’ work easier and more efficient. Those who work for small and rural governments have said previously that the technology has given them “breathing room.” Others argued that focusing on AI’s benefits will help sell it more to the public.

Cheney said a lot of work lies ahead on FOIA requests, and that automation is the key, and getting staff to recognize AI is not going away. She said the city has to figure out ways of being smarter and how it is addressing the demands it is seeing now. Matelski said government must recognize that the technology is here to stay and embrace it carefully, with boundaries on it. The articles leave open whether state and local governments will follow the federal government’s lead on the rebrand. The articles also leave open how the automation of FOIA processes will proceed.

Articles.Title: Does state-and-local AI need a rebrand? - Route Fifty

stories.Headline: Apple partners with OpenEvidence to study AI health answers in 200,000 users
stories.Summary:
Apple launched a new research application on November 15, 2026, to study how people utilize artificial intelligence for health purposes. The company is partnering with a healthcare-focused AI firm called OpenEvidence to conduct this extensive scientific study. This initiative aims to understand how answers grounded in clinical data can assist users with their medical questions. The project will involve up to 200,000 participants over a period of more than 12 months.

To join the study, users must be in the United States and over 21 years of age. Participants are required to use an iPhone 15 or a newer model running iOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence enabled. The app provides simplified answers based on sources like Nature, the Journal of the American Medical Association, and The New England Journal of Medicine. Users can share HealthKit data, including sleep and resting heart rate, to receive more personalized suggestions.

Sumbul Desai, the vice president of Health and Fitness at Apple, stated that responsible innovation requires scientific rigor and clinical grounding. She explained that a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful method to understand how people evaluate health AI in daily life. Desai believes the resulting insights will help the company build trusted tools that support people throughout their health journeys. The company noted that data will be anonymized and not used to train any AI models.

The application allows users to rate responses, provide feedback, and participate in monthly surveys to improve the system. It also guides users toward specific medical providers for concerning issues and helps them prepare for doctor visits. OpenEvidence deletes all query and response data after 24 hours to maintain privacy for the participants. It remains uncertain if Apple intends to integrate these AI answering capabilities into Siri or the existing Health app.

Articles.Title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health

stories.Headline: UKRI funds 20 Turing AI Fellows with over £39 million to tackle medicine, energy and nuclear safety
stories.Summary:
UK Research and Innovation announced 20 new Turing AI Fellows on 16 November 2026, backed by more than £39 million in government funding. The fellows will use artificial intelligence to tackle challenges including personalised medicine, clean energy and nuclear safety. The cohort includes 17 researchers supported through the Turing AI Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships and three supported through the Turing AI Global Fellowships. Both schemes are delivered by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council and form part of UKRI's Industrial Strategy 8 AI Priority Programme. The fellowships contribute to UKRI's wider investment of more than £11 billion in the UK's highest-potential sectors.

The Turing AI Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships started in October 2026 and will run for three years, while the Turing AI Global Fellowships start in 2027 and will run for five years. Dr Thiago Sogo Bezerra of King's College London will combine AI with novel detector technology to improve neutrino measurements, with potential applications for nuclear reactor monitoring and safety. Dr Roisin Buckley of the University of Glasgow will develop AI tools to improve understanding of underground and seabed conditions, supporting cleaner energy and major infrastructure projects. Professor Neil Cummins of the London School of Economics and Political Science will use AI to unlock more than a million handwritten wills. Professor Jocelyn Monroe of the University of Oxford will use the search for dark matter to develop more trustworthy AI systems capable of identifying extremely rare events.

Professor Charlotte Deane, Senior Responsible Owner for the UKRI IS8 AI Programme and Executive Chair of EPSRC, said AI has enormous potential to transform how society understands and tackles its biggest challenges. She said the fellowships will give outstanding researchers the freedom and support to push the boundaries of AI itself while applying it in new ways across disciplines. She said they are part of UKRI's long-term commitment to AI, building on sustained investment that helps strengthen the UK's position as a global leader. She said that by investing in exceptional people and ideas, UKRI is helping build the expertise and capability the UK needs to remain at the forefront of AI research and innovation. She said this will turn advances in AI to advance knowledge, improve lives and drive growth across the UK.

Dr Jonathan Phillips of the University of Exeter will combine AI and experimental biology to help scientists better understand and design proteins for applications in medicine, biotechnology and environmental sensing. Professor Michael Tadao Inouye of the University of Cambridge will use AI and large-scale health data to better understand disease and support more personalised healthcare. The new fellows join a growing Turing AI Fellowships community that has already helped launch start-up companies, attract significant investment, influence policy, and train the next generation of AI researchers. The application of AI across disciplines will support growth and high-skilled jobs across the UK while building on areas of established UK strength and global leadership. The cohort will help ensure the UK remains at the forefront of both AI research.

The funded projects include AI-driven precision measurements and applications in neutrino physics, led by Dr Thiago Sogo Bezerra at King's College London. Professor Cristian Bonato of Heriot-Watt University leads work on developing a real-time AI-enhanced experimenter for quantum sensing. Professor Jasmin Fisher of University College London leads work on understanding cancer through trustworthy AI and digital twins. Dr Katherine Inzani of the University of Nottingham leads atoms to devices, machine learning approaches for the dynamics of functional materials. Professor Sally Keith of Lancaster University leads BEACON, behavioural ecology AI for conservation action.

Professor Nan Li of Imperial College London leads work on manufacturable-by-design to production-ready, sustainable and trustworthy AI for materials forming. Professor Qiuhua Liang of Loughborough University leads HiPA-flood, high performance computing and AI for personalised flood forecasting and resilient futures. Professor Andrea Manica of the University of Cambridge leads work on predicting future biodiversity changes by integrating multiple lines of evidence at scale. Dr Jacob Page of The University of Edinburgh leads work on a new era for turbulence computation. Professor Ganna Pogrebna of Queen's University Belfast leads BIQUAD, behaviourally informed quantum-augmented AI agents for bias-aware human-machine collaboration in critical domains.

Professor Matthew Rigby of the University of Bristol leads a near-real time global greenhouse gas observation and emissions evaluation system. Professor Corwin Wright of the University of Bath leads a gravity wave latent inference framework for climate. Professor Jonathan May is relocating from the US, from the University of Southern California, to The University of Edinburgh to lead work on from language to intent. Professor Denny Wu is relocating from the US, from New York University and the Flatiron Institute, to the University of Oxford to lead work on a predictive mathematical foundation for scalable deep learning. Professor Roi Reichart is relocating from Israel, from Technion, Israel Institute of Technology, to the University of Cambridge to lead work on building socially intelligent AI, core AI advances for modelling behavior, interaction, and emotion.

stories.Headline: Egypt health minister discusses deploying AI for 100 Million Healthy Lives initiative
stories.Summary:
Egypt's Minister of Health and Population, Dr. Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, met on Monday, November 16, 2026, to discuss strengthening collaboration and bringing the latest digital technologies into the country's healthcare system, according to a ministry spokesperson. The meeting looked at ways to develop an artificial intelligence framework for healthcare and to expand cooperation in digital health, the spokesperson, Dr. Hossam Abdel Ghaffar, said. Talks also covered proposed infrastructure and technological solutions for building integrated health systems and for making telemedicine services easier for patients to use. The discussions further explored using big data and the digital infrastructure Egypt has built in recent years, combined with advanced operational models, to streamline medical data flows and support informed healthcare decisions.

The meeting examined how to deploy AI applications in support of the "100 Million Healthy Lives" presidential public health initiative, the spokesperson said. By drawing on the large national health databases generated through these programs, the ministry aims to improve diagnostic accuracy, enable early prediction of disease and identify groups at high risk. The minister stressed the need to speed up coordination and executive action between ministry officials and private-sector representatives so that cooperation frameworks can be put into operation. He said harnessing available capabilities and expertise would support development of the national healthcare system and drive a major improvement in the quality and efficiency of medical services provided to citizens.

The meeting was attended by Deputy Minister of Health and Population Dr. Mohamed El-Tayeb and Assistant Minister for Public Health Initiatives Dr. Mohamed Hassani. Others present were Assistant Minister for National Projects Dr. Sherif Mostafa and Head of the Central Administration for Healthcare Quality Dr. Galal El-Shishini. The Head of the Central Administration for the Health and Population Information Center, Eng. Ahmed Sobhy, attended, along with Dr. Mona Khalifa, General Director of the General Administration for Presidential Initiatives. The articles do not say what steps follow the meeting or when any of the discussed systems would be introduced.

stories.Headline: Daisytuner raises 6 million euros to automate AI performance engineering across different chips
stories.Summary:
The German deep tech startup Daisytuner announced that it raised 6 million euros in seed funding on November 16, 2026. This funding round was co-led by Elaia and LEA Ventures, with additional participation from Seedcamp and the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund. The company intends to use these funds to expand its compiler technology, grow its internal team, and bring its Daisyflow platform to more enterprises. This technology automates performance engineering to ensure AI models run at maximum speed on any available chip.

The company will utilize its patented optimization platform and a self-learning compiler to eliminate the need for manual integration. This process converts code from frameworks like PyTorch into native code for various architectures, including AMD and Nvidia GPUs. The Daisyflow platform is already live in production and has shown that Qwen 2.5 can run 18 percent faster on AMD Instinct GPUs than the industry standard vLLM. Founded in 2024 by Adrian Schmitz and Lukas Trümper, the firm relies on research from institutions like ETH Zurich and TU Munich.

CEO Lukas Trümper stated that software currently keeps many available accelerators on the sidelines despite growing demand for compute. He noted that the company is collaborating with European hyperscalers, enterprises, and chip vendors to ensure new hardware enters production immediately. Sébastien Lefebvre of Elaia remarked that the industry needs to remove the bottleneck created by relying on a single vendor's software stack. Alexi Malikotsinas from LEA Ventures added that the technology restores control over compute efficiency and technology sovereignty to the customers.

stories.Headline: FleetGuru develops AI agents that assess repair quotes in seconds using historical maintenance data
stories.Summary:
Australian fleet maintenance technology provider FleetGuru.ai says its platform automatically approves an average of 35% of maintenance jobs, rising to 70% for some customers. The company is developing AI agents that can assess repair quotes in seconds, using historical maintenance data to check whether proposed work and charges meet fleet approval rules. The technology aims to reduce the time spent reviewing maintenance requests and identify excessive repair charges before work is authorised. FleetGuru founder and managing director Eden Shirley disclosed the figures at the Fleet APAC Summit in Bangkok in June, where he also outlined plans to expand into Japan. FleetGuru has not specified how many of those approvals are handled by AI agents.

FleetGuru is developing maintenance data infrastructure for the Japanese market, building on its operations in Australia and New Zealand. US-based Fleetio made its AI Service Advisor generally available in September following a six-month trial. Fleetio says the system assessed more than US$1.4 billion in maintenance expenditure during the trial, helping vehicles return to service an average of 2.5 hours sooner per repair. The technology can also approve low-risk repairs automatically within limits set by fleet managers. An April 2026 Fleetio survey of more than 600 fleet professionals found that only 4.1% supported AI making high-impact decisions, including automated approvals, without human authorisation.

Barry Pryce, FleetGuru's CTO and tech co-founder, says reviewing maintenance quotes is one of the first fleet management tasks where AI agents can outperform humans. Pryce says AI agents can complete these checks in seconds, identifying pricing discrepancies that fleet managers might otherwise miss. He says an agent compares every line item against billions of data points, and that a human cannot analyse at the same speed and scale. Pryce says the AI agent works from structured historical maintenance data and does not answer from a general model's memory or the internet. He says FleetGuru has billions of data points captured from vehicle records, service history, workshop and parts pricing and policy rules.

Pryce says fleet managers can set the rules governing which repairs AI agents are allowed to approve, including limits on expenditure and supplier restrictions. He says anything outside those limits triggers human review, and every decision is logged with the data behind it so a manager can override it. Pryce says FleetGuru starts with low-risk, high-volume decisions and widens the agent's authority as the results prove out. He says FleetGuru processes close to 1 million work orders per annum, totalling hundreds of millions in maintenance costs. Pryce says cost savings vary by fleet, and even small percentage gains compound quickly.

The April 2026 Fleetio survey also found that just 1.5% of fleet professionals said they fully trusted AI-generated recommendations without human review. Pryce says the biggest barrier to wider adoption of AI maintenance approvals is proving they deliver financial savings. He says fleet managers have heard plenty of promises and are right to want evidence before handing over decisions that cost money. Pryce says the top concerns of fleet managers today are rising costs and increasing regulation. He says maintenance management is expensive and resource-intensive, and it is easy to demonstrate real savings on invoices and the time required to review and approve them.

FleetGuru has yet to provide specific figures showing how much its AI agents can reduce maintenance costs. Pryce says FleetGuru's quote scrutiny engine uses machine learning to analyse historical maintenance data and assess repair costs, rather than relying on generative AI. He says FleetGuru works primarily through fleet management companies, integrating its services with the systems their customers already use. Pryce says a telematics provider would need years to build the supplier network behind maintenance transaction data. He says the AI projects that fail will be the ones that don't deliver ROI and don't own their own data or service networks, and that FleetGuru owns both.

stories.Headline: i14 raises $9m from IP Group to build brain-inspired, energy-efficient AI models
stories.Summary:
i14, an artificial intelligence company led by chief executive Tom McLeod, has raised a $9 million funding round backed by IP Group PLC, the two sides announced in an interview with Proactive published on 16 November 2026. McLeod and Eeshan Kulkarni, a principal at IP Group, spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the company's work on energy-efficient AI models and its plans to scale the technology. The company says it is developing new AI architectures inspired by the human brain, which are designed to deliver frontier-level intelligence while using less memory, computing power and energy than conventional large language models. McLeod said the technology can keep energy and memory costs consistent as models process more information, which could remove the traditional trade-off between capability and efficiency.

The $9 million round is intended to fund product development, expansion of the team and deeper partnerships with hyperscalers, neocloud providers and AI inference platforms, including work involving AWS. Over the next 12 to 18 months, i14 aims to broaden its model offering, grow early customer adoption and make the technology more widely available. The company says wider availability could give businesses and governments greater control over their AI capabilities while requiring less computing infrastructure. IP Group, which is listed on the London Stock Exchange under the ticker IPO, backed the round through its focus on deep technology and the future of computing.

Kulkarni explained that IP Group backed the funding round because of i14's scientific innovation, its research expertise and its commercial potential. He also described how the company fits into IP Group's wider deep-tech portfolio and its focus on the future of computing. McLeod set out the company's view that its brain-inspired designs could cut the memory, computing power and energy that large language models demand. Proactive noted that it has a commercial relationship with IP Group PLC and that the article was produced independently under its editorial standards policy.

The interview was published by Proactive, which covers artificial intelligence, deep technology, investment and emerging companies across its news and video channels. The articles do not say when the funding round closed, who else took part or what valuation the round placed on i14. They also do not give a date for the AWS work or say how far it has progressed. Beyond the 12 to 18 month goals described by McLeod, the articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: i14 targets more efficient AI as IP Group backs $9m funding round

stories.Headline: Mercor raises $750 million at a $20 billion valuation to train AI models
stories.Summary:
Mercor secured $750 million in a Series D at a $20 billion valuation, with Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, Nvidia and Apollo-affiliated funds among the participants. The San Francisco company, originally an AI hiring platform, now connects technology firms with subject-matter experts who help train and test AI models. Traversal joined the unicorn ranks with a $120 million Series B co-led by Kleiner Perkins, Redpoint Ventures and Khosla Ventures. Nooks secured a $500 million commitment from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund, with the investor taking a share of the returns generated by its capital rather than equity. Fractile, based in London and Bristol, reached a $7 billion valuation after a $720 million Series C led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint.

Fractile’s round included backing from the UK’s Sovereign AI fund and the British Business Bank, and its first commercial chip is due next year. In Germany, Sparxity, formerly SpiNNcloud, closed a Series A led by ICM HPQC Fund, with participation from Lockheed Martin Ventures, GlobalFoundries and the EIC Fund, bringing total funding secured by its team to $90 million. Pure Data Centres Group agreed a US$780 million growth facility with a US$1.1 billion accordion that could lift total financing to around US$1.9 billion. Physicl raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital to generate targeted training data for the edge cases where models fail, working with labs including Meta and World Labs. Tel Aviv-based Bay emerged from stealth with $50 million in total funding, including a $37 million Series A led by Battery Ventures.

Bay’s platform evaluates each agent action in the context of the full session and decides in milliseconds whether it can proceed, and the company counts Micron, Peloton, ClickUp and Wix as customers. Finite State secured $27 million in Series C funding led by The O.H.I.O. Fund to help device makers find vulnerabilities in connected products. Ocient closed a $100 million Series C co-led by BOKA Capital and OCA Ventures to let agents and analysts query petabyte-scale data with built-in governance over agent access and lineage. Ballistic Ventures is seeking $490 million across two new funds, according to SEC filings. Berlin’s Pliant raised an $80 million Series C led by Seaya Nova and Speedinvest to open its B2B payment infrastructure to AI agents, letting tools such as Claude and ChatGPT connect via Model Context Protocol.

Toronto-based Blue J secured US$176 million at a US$700 million valuation, led by JMI Equity, to commercialise its AI tax research agent and expand into the UK, with nearly US$100 million to fund a secondary sale for employees and early investors. Kalepa raised a $75 million Series B at a $470 million valuation to coordinate agents across underwriting, pricing and portfolio management. Seattle’s Finpilot raised a $10 million Series A led by Lobby Capital for its agent-driven operating system for institutional investors. London’s Crediflow AI secured £1.5 million to automate commercial loan analysis. Athena took $2.5 million in pre-seed funding from a16z Speedrun to deliver commercial real estate legal work at a fixed fee per transaction, with agents drafting redlines before attorneys sign off.

Mercor’s valuation roughly doubles the $10 billion it reached last October, as AI startups took $102 billion in Q3 2026, or 64% of global venture capital. Traversal’s technology maps production systems into a form AI agents can read, letting them test thousands of hypotheses in parallel to find the root cause of software incidents, and monthly investigations have grown more than 100-fold this year to nearly 73,000. Nooks said it is on track to nearly triple annual recurring revenue by year end. Fractile is building chips designed to make inference faster, cheaper and less energy-intensive. Sparxity’s sparse-native chips target up to 44 times faster inference in ultra-sparse models.

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said the government wants to stop world-leading UK ideas from becoming industries elsewhere. Pure Data Centres Executive Chairman and interim CEO Gary Wojtaszek said power is the biggest limit on AI growth, and the company secures it before building capacity. Finite State CEO Matt Wyckhouse said AI-equipped attackers can now find flaws faster than manufacturers can identify affected products. Ocient expects to more than triple revenue this year. A JPMorgan Chase report found AI-enabled companies made up about 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals through May, up from 36% in 2019.

Pliant has passed $100 million in ARR and is positioning its licensed status as a principal Visa and Mastercard member as an advantage once agents begin moving money. Kalepa has tripled revenue while remaining cash flow positive. Bay is less than a year old. The week’s largest venture deal went to a company that sits behind the agent economy rather than selling agents directly. Investors backed the companies building, securing and powering AI agents, from a $20 billion valuation for an agent-training platform to fresh bets on inference chips, agent security and specialist tools for finance, insurance, tax and law. The common thread is a market paying for AI that does real work inside real businesses.

Valuations remain high, and many of these companies have yet to prove durable margins at scale. The growing emphasis on revenue growth, customer retention and cash flow suggests investors are rewarding AI that can show measurable commercial results. Agent security is becoming its own investment category, financing structures are diversifying beyond conventional equity, as Nooks and Blue J show, and sovereign infrastructure ambitions are increasingly shaping where chip capital lands. Capital flowed to every layer the idea requires, with Mercor and Physicl supplying the data and evaluation that make agents reliable. Fractile, Sparxity and Pure DC provide the compute and power to run them, Bay and Finite State address the security risks they create, and vertical players from Pliant to Kalepa put them to work in regulated industries.

stories.Headline: Baidu AI cloud growth offsets a 22 percent drop in search advertising revenue
stories.Summary:
Baidu reported its third-quarter financial results on Monday, November 16, showing a slight decline in overall revenue. The company saw total revenue drop by 1% from the previous year to RMB30.8 billion, which equals approximately 4.60 billion dollars. This decline was largely driven by a 10% fall in revenue from the streaming arm, iQIYI, which brought in RMB6.0 billion. Meanwhile, the core online marketing business suffered a significant 22% slump, falling to RMB11.9 billion.

The company is shifting its focus toward AI, with AI-powered segments now making up 53% of General Business revenue. General Business revenue grew 1% to RMB25.0 billion, supported by AI segments that earned RMB13.2 billion. Specifically, AI Cloud Infra revenue reached RMB8.2 billion, while GPU cloud revenue surged by 191% from a year earlier. However, this growth requires massive investment, leaving the company with a negative free cash flow of RMB4.6 billion.

CEO Robin Li stated that the company's full-stack AI investments are creating meaningful growth for the business. He noted that AI Cloud Infra has evolved into a major driver of revenue for the organization. Despite these gains, AI-native marketing services fell 15% to RMB2.4 billion, and AI Applications remained flat at RMB2.6 billion. This suggests that the company is currently succeeding more as a provider of compute power than as a creator of consumer AI products.

The company continues to face a difficult balance between shrinking ad revenue and expensive infrastructure costs. Net income attributable to Baidu was RMB1.4 billion, while non-GAAP net income stood at RMB2.4 billion. The business must stabilize its search advertising losses to improve its cash flow position in the future. Baidu will continue pushing its Ernie model to maintain a position among the top tier of AI models.

Articles.Title: Baidu's AI cloud surge nearly cancels out a 22% slump in search ads

stories.Headline: Zhengzhou University researchers find AI-integrated teaching improves ophthalmology trainee scores
stories.Summary:
Researchers at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University conducted a randomized trial to evaluate a new AI-supported instruction model for ophthalmology clinical teaching. Between June 2023 and June 2025, the study tracked 106 medical trainees to see if restructuring education around job competency produced measurable gains. The investigators used a random number table to divide the participants into an observation group of 53 trainees and a control group of 53 trainees. This two-year evaluation compared traditional lecture-based methods against a curriculum that integrated artificial intelligence tools into problem-based and case-based learning.

The new framework required integrating AI directly into case-based and problem-based learning formats while focusing specifically on job competency development. To measure success, the team used the Chinese Clinical Physician Post Competency Questionnaire, the Critical Thinking Disposition Inventory-Chinese Version, and the Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise. The results showed that the observation group achieved significantly higher scores in theoretical knowledge, practical skills, and clinical performance, with statistical significance established at P < 0.05. These trainees also reported greater overall satisfaction with their teaching experience and showed improved critical thinking compared to the control group.

The authors, Zhipeng W. and Long L., concluded that this AI-integrated model was associated with higher short-term scores across all evaluated parameters. They noted that the study was limited by its single-center design, a relatively small sample size of 106 people, and a short intervention duration. Because the model combined several different elements, the researchers stated it was difficult to isolate the specific contribution of each individual component. They emphasized that further multicenter studies with longer follow-up periods are necessary to determine if these educational benefits can be sustained and generalized.

Articles.Title: AI-Integrated Competency Teaching Improves Short-Term Ophthalmology Scores in Randomized Trial

stories.Headline: Cmpnd releases dspy-wsp to enable weight-space programming for DSPy
stories.Summary:
Cmpnd released a prototype optimizer called dspy-wsp on November 14, 2026, to bring weight-space programming to DSPy. This new tool allows a frontier large language model to read and edit the weights of another model directly. The process avoids the use of training loops, fine-tuning datasets, or gradients. Cmpnd tested the system using GPT-6-Astra calls, which cost between 5 and 10 dollars to improve various decision models.

The software is available under the MIT license and requires DSPy 3.5 for installation via pip. It was tested on open decision models ranging from 0.6B to 9B parameters, including the d1-omni-600M and Clef-Flash models. Experiments ran on a single Mac, where 2B models used 6 GB of memory and the d1-omni-600M required at least 4 GB. Performance gains on Typed Decisions ranged from 1.9 to 16.1 points with WeightSpace alone, and up to 20.0 points when combined with ReAnchor.

The research team explained that weight-space programming treats neural network weights as a program that can be rewritten through reasoning. They stated that a writer model forms a hypothesis about specific neurons and writes code to patch them. This method differs from prompt optimization, which only edits text, and fine-tuning, which relies on gradient descent. The developers noted that while the tool is a cheap and verifiable way to edit models, it remains very experimental and slow.

This technology builds upon MIT research which suggests that reasoning can now reach weights directly rather than just optimizing text. The team demonstrated that Astra could identify games from policy networks and fix broken car-on-ramp policies. They also improved Qwen3.5-0.8B math scores by changing a small fraction of its weights. However, the research indicates that editing can remove existing obstacles but cannot add entirely new abilities to a model.

Articles.Title: Cmpnd Releases dspy-wsp: Weight-Space Programming Comes to DSPy

stories.headline_source: Cmpnd Releases dspy-wsp: Weight-Space Programming Comes to DSPy

stories.Headline: Vercel Labs releases UI SDK with over 50 interface behaviors for coding agents
stories.Summary:
Vercel Labs released UI SDK, an open-source beta library of interface behaviors built for coding agents, on November 12, 2026. The library is headless, meaning it ships behaviors rather than finished components, and agents combine those behaviors into accessible components for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components. It contains more than 50 behaviors, 51 component modules in the repository and 6 npm packages at version 0.1.0-beta.1. The packages are published under Apache-2.0 and run on any modern browser without a GPU, requiring React 19+, Vue 3.5+, Svelte 5.33+, Solid 2 RC or plain Web Components. The README lists keyboard navigation, focus, selection, dismissal, popups, drag and drop and the ARIA they need, all living in @ui-sdk/core with thin adapters rendering it in each framework.

Components start as primitives defined with definePrimitive, which declares state, an API and slots, and each framework then renders the primitive with createParts so one behavior definition can serve a React app and a Svelte app. Setup is a prompt pasted into an agent that installs the packages and adds a note to AGENTS.md pointing to the ui-sdk skill and to llms.txt inside the package docs. The docs group behaviors into 10 categories, from Focus and Keys to Canvas, and prebuilt components include Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Menu, Tree and Color Picker. The agent docs describe a bridge created with createAgent() before the page renders, where agent.snapshot() lists components, their state and available actions and agent.act() runs an action such as renaming a project with setValue. Apps can pass an allow callback to approve or refuse actions, change callbacks receive source "agent" and can cancel the change, and tools can also be registered with supported browsers through WebMCP.

Vercel compared its bridge against browser tools on one project-settings task in which the agent renamed a project, updated members and notification settings, then saved, with both agents using Sonnet through Claude Code and the same task and system prompt. Figures are medians of 3 runs: tool calls fell from 16 to 5, a 69% drop, text read fell from 39.8k to 6.8k characters, a drop of 83%, time fell 61% from 41 s to 16 s, and cost fell 56% from $0.073 to $0.032. Vercel cautions that the figures should be treated as directional, because the sample is one task and the browser-tools run used a different component library, and it does not name the Sonnet version. The project site explains the idea with a Select: instead of handing the agent a finished Select, you hand it a popup, a selection model and typeahead, and those same parts can produce an autocomplete, a combobox or a component nobody has designed yet. The README example builds a search field with createFocusRecovery whose Clear button appears only when there is text, and pages without a build step can load web.js and web.css from ui-sdk.dev per the skill listing.

Articles.Title: Vercel Releases UI SDK: 50+ UI Behaviors for AI Coding Agents

stories.headline_source: Vercel Releases UI SDK: 50+ UI Behaviors for AI Coding Agents

stories.Headline: 36Kr highlights 10 little-known AI tools that target office tasks and could grow fast
stories.Summary:
The article, published by 36Kr on 2026-11-12 at 07:25, presents 10 AI tools that have only hundreds to thousands of users, mostly spread in Reddit posts and niche communities, and that the article says are likely to see explosive growth soon. The piece is a translated article by Shen Translation, a translation team under 36Kr that focuses on technology, business, workplace and life and introduces new foreign technologies, perspectives and industry trends. The article's editor's note says AI tools iterate at an extremely fast pace and that by the time a tool goes viral the early-mover advantage has long vanished. The article says the 10 tools target real office pain points covering scenarios from meetings and data analysis to note management, for users who want to take the lead in improving work efficiency. The article says people using these tools now can clear their inbox in just 15 minutes, finish sorting a list of potential customers that used to take a whole day in a few seconds, and even abandon multiple paid software they used before.

Napkin AI lets a user describe a process, funnel model or comparison relationship in one sentence and automatically generates concise, beautiful visual charts, with no manual dragging of boxes or struggling to adjust SmartArt in PPT. Enterprise founders often use Napkin AI to turn long strategic texts into funnel diagrams in seconds, and the tool is built for people who have a clear idea in mind that turns messy when written on paper. Granola runs silently in the background of meetings, does not appear in the participant list, and organizes conversation into well-structured notes, meeting resolutions and to-do items, unlike most meeting transcription tools that send a prompt as soon as they join the call and make all participants constrained. Granola can save an hour of workload unconsciously for people with many customer communication meetings and interviews every week. Fyxer automatically categorizes received emails, writes replies in the user's tone and generates follow-up emails, is embedded directly in Gmail and Outlook with no need to switch software, and many users report freeing up nearly an extra hour every day.

Clay grabs information from hundreds of data sources, relies on the AI intelligent agent named "Claygent" to mine and supplement information in batches, and personalizes potential customer profiles, and the article says Clay is the secret weapon behind business customer development work that seems well researched and highly efficient. For people in sales and freelance customer development, entering the query instruction can replace a whole day of manual data collection work. Gumloop is a drag-and-drop automation construction tool that connects various applications to each other and directly connects applications to large AI models, letting teams build zero-code workflows such as reading every newly submitted form, generating a content summary and assigning it to the corresponding person in charge. The article says Gumloop found a perfect positioning, neither too high-threshold for ordinary users nor too lackluster with few practical functions. The open-source, locally deployable n8n is offered as an alternative for people troubled by Zapier's billing model, in which you pay more for each additional step in the workflow.

With n8n you can build the logic of "if condition A is met, execute B" while all calculations run in an environment under your full control, with no continuously rising billing bills, though it has a higher learning threshold than out-of-the-box SaaS software. The article says people who often deal with repetitive automation work will soon be rewarded for the time spent learning n8n. Wispr Flow converts speech into well-formatted text in real time, fast enough that many people write emails and documents by speaking instead of typing, and it automatically removes filler words, slips of the tongue and pauses so the output does not read like a rigid recording transcription. Wispr Flow suits people whose thinking speed is faster than their typing speed, bridging the efficiency gap between thinking and text output. The eighth tool lets a user upload a spreadsheet and ask questions in plain language, such as "What caused the data decline in March?"

or "Generate charts by region", and it completes the analysis and generates visual charts with no pivot tables or memorized function formulas. The eighth tool is designed for people who can understand business data but do not want to spend energy struggling with Excel. Firecrawl converts any web page into clean structured data for AI: feeding a web page directly to an AI tool often yields messy, invalid text mixing navigation bars, advertisements and disordered layouts, and Firecrawl returns clean, well-organized content from a single web page address or an entire site, suiting research or building a retrievable knowledge base. Firecrawl belongs to the underlying supporting tools, running silently in the background of many other products, so it is rarely mentioned by the public.

Mem automatically establishes associations between related ideas in notes, so when a related topic appears again an inspiration from three months ago emerges automatically instead of requiring an active search. Mem's user experience differs completely from ordinary note-taking software: it reduces manual archiving and classification, focuses on information recall and simulates the operation mode of human memory. The article says every few months a previously little-known tool suddenly becomes a hit and sparks heated discussions in every Slack community, but by the time it becomes a popular choice the advantage of early access has long been gone. The article's editor's note says the tools it introduces have not yet gained widespread popularity and are perfect for users who want to take the lead in improving work efficiency.

The article says the tools are available to start using right now, with no need to sign up for courses, join communities or wait in line for beta access. The article says all that is really needed is to spend ten minutes trying the tools before they become popular all over the internet. The article gives no further details on pricing, company ownership or launch dates for the 10 tools. stories.Headline: AI variety shows emerge as a new industry trend to reduce costs and fill daily entertainment needs
stories.Summary:
AI variety shows emerged as a new industry trend during 2026 to reduce production costs. These programs use artificial intelligence to fill the daily entertainment needs of fragmented users. Some creators use AI to generate characters, scenes, and plot trends for short video platforms. Other mainstream media outlets embed AI as a technical tool within traditional production frameworks. This shift allows the industry to address high costs and insufficient production capacity.

The AI-native path requires only several people and costs several thousand yuan per episode. This contrasts with traditional shows that cost millions and require dozens of staff members. China Media Group launched six AI programs in 2026, including Singing Competition with AI Singers. The Win in AI+ program gathered 611 teams and signed investment intentions totaling 1.23 billion yuan. AI penetration in editing for top 2026 shows exceeded 70 percent, increasing efficiency by 30 to 40 percent.

Industry observers say AI variety shows are becoming standardized fast-moving consumer goods for the public. They argue these shows provide commercial certainty unlike the gambling nature of AI short dramas. The creator 100,000 Challenges shifted to AI and gained millions of followers in half a year. This creator reports that commercial orders for AI content reach between 80,000 and 150,000 yuan. Brands benefit because virtual characters do not face the risk of public image collapse.

Viewers are affected by the split between emotional luxury goods and efficient AI content. Fans of the 12 Star Trainee Competition formed data support stations for virtual contestants. This show recorded over 250 million topic views one month after its initial launch. Meanwhile, Mango TV's Friendship Later reached a 77.1 percent market share using real human empathy. This proves that authentic human nature remains the sharpest weapon for reality variety shows.

The articles state that AI short dramas reached a market size of 220 billion yuan. However, 90 percent of companies in that sector are losing money due to overcapacity. AI variety shows have a higher production threshold because they require complex content planning. They replicate mature categories like romance, workplace games, and talent competitions to attract users. This allows them to build IP value through personas rather than one-time plot consumption.

Next, AI will continue moving from a backstage production tool to a frontstage protagonist. Long-video platforms will likely maintain a steady integration of AI into their existing workflows. Short-video platforms have already established a commercial closed loop for pure AI content. The articles leave open whether the AI talent show track can survive recent removals. It remains unclear if AI variety shows will eventually shake the core of reality shows.

Token packages went on sale during the Double 11 shopping festival in November 2026. These products appeared on e-commerce platforms and in livestreaming rooms for consumers. This trend follows a boom in artificial intelligence inference across the industry. New changes are now affecting the upstream and downstream segments of the industrial chain. These developments reflect a shift where inference is becoming the mainstream study of AI.

JD.com saw Token package sales increase 20 times month-on-month during a November 2 livestream. From October 30 to November 1, bundled AI computer sales on JD.com rose 100 percent. Austin Li sold 100,000 Qianwen Office cards, totaling 2 trillion Tokens, in thirty minutes on November 2. Tmall AI Space Station features models from Qianwen, Zhipu, MiniMax, and Qoder. JD Cloud and Volcano Engine also offer products in a new AI software recharge hall.

Intel China Chairman Wang Zhicong said more computing power will deploy on the inference side. He believes this will extend to devices closer to the edge over five years. Qualcomm's Wan Weixing stated that end-side AI is evolving toward agent experiences like task orchestration. UCloud's Liu Hua believes cloud service delivery units are shifting toward the Token. State Information Center official Wang Jiandong suggested unifying token measurement and establishing conversion standards.

Ordinary consumers are affected by varying model capabilities and unclear refund rules for Token quotas. Some buyers reported that gray market stores have falsely marked traffic and high costs. These unregulated AI transfer stations operate without public filing information or clear operating entities. Users face risks including privacy leakage, malicious implantation, and unprotected data transmission. Some customers noted that low-priced channels suffer from server congestion and frequent disconnections.

China Center for Information Industry Development data shows inference data volume now exceeds training data volume. Daily average token call volume surpassed 175 trillion by June, 1000 times higher than early 2024. AMD released the Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 series in September 2026 for local model running. MediaTek and NVIDIA designed the RTX Spark superchip for Windows 11 PCs from six brands. AMD reported shipping over 500,000 agent PCs capable of running 100-billion-parameter models.

Intel may implement green computing power warehouses in the first half of next year. These warehouses will convert green power into inference Tokens for distribution through networks. The industry continues to move agent capabilities from the cloud to local device processing. Articles leave open how the government will standardize billing disclosure and third-party verification. stories.Headline: AI music replaces human songs in playlists as low cost tracks surge on domestic platforms
stories.Summary:
AI music is replacing human songs in playlists as low cost tracks surge on domestic platforms during 2026. This shift occurred over the past year as AI generated content began flooding the music industry. Many artists cannot be verified because they lack recording studios or records of live performances. The number of new daily tracks rose from 70,000 to over 100,000. More than 20 percent of these new songs are created by AI.

The technology allows clients to cut original quotations from 5,000 yuan down to 300 yuan. For 300 yuan, a client can now get 10 different versions of a song. One tone deaf girl in a county town earned 3,000 yuan by writing songs. An AI music MV called Veterans gained 120 million views in half a month. This video featured 10 ancient historical figures who were made to speak.

Zhang Guangyi, a musician for 15 years, said AI is a sharp tool for craftsmanship. He noted that AI provides an 80 point rough draft for his work. Zhang believes that humans no longer have an absolute advantage in final listening experience. He stated that tools change, but ears and aesthetics do not change. He now teaches both conservatory students and amateurs who use AI.

A music critic who listened for 11 years gave AI a second highest score. Mid tier musicians are the most painful group because they face replacement by processes. Some peers of Zhang switched to wedding photography or teaching piano to children. Others completely quit the industry as their commissions decreased by half over two years. Clients now prioritize stability and no mistakes over emotion or soul.

Zhang Guangyi graduated from a Computer English major at a conservatory of music. He worked in Beijing before becoming an independent musician in 2018. He rented a 40 square meter studio in his hometown for various commissions. He once arranged 22 songs in one month during his most prosperous days. He previously viewed AI as a soulless technology that erased his experience.

Zhang now uses AI to lay out structure and style for his commissions. He focuses on the final 20 percent of a song to add human touch. He recently took a film scoring commission that required real instruments for decisive sections. The articles leave open whether the music industry will completely disappear. They do not state if other musicians will adopt AI tools.

stories.Headline: Anthropic expands Claude office tools with Sheets and Whiteboards as Microsoft shares fall
stories.Summary:
Anthropic announced on Tuesday, November 12, 2026, that it is expanding Claude's office functions with a spreadsheet called Claude Sheets, a digital whiteboard called Claude Whiteboards, and upgrades to its data analysis tool Claude Data and its interactive connectors. Together with the existing document, presentation and design features, the company said this further shapes Claude's office product ecosystem. After the news that Claude was coming, Microsoft, the developer of the Office suite, plunged more than 3% in intraday trading before the decline narrowed and the stock closed down 2.2%. Anthropic is also pushing for a US stock IPO, according to the report.

According to the announcement, users can build spreadsheets, organize data, and create and edit formulas together with colleagues and Claude, collaborating across multiple worksheets. Nicholas Lin, Head of Product at Anthropic, told the media that the current Claude Sheets experience is still quite basic and is not aimed at complex tasks such as financial modeling, where using Anthropic's plug-in for existing spreadsheet software would be more effective. Claude Whiteboards is aimed at team discussions and project planning, letting teams place and organize ideas on a shared board and then have Claude summarize the discussion results. Claude Data, formerly Claude Dashboards, can connect to tools such as Snowflake and Salesforce and generate dashboards, visual analysis and short videos with voiceover. Anthropic also previewed a meeting assistant called Claude Meetings, which users will be able to add to calls so it records content and updates documents during the discussion.

Lin said that products from Microsoft and Google have their own applicable scenarios, especially for more complex enterprise-level applications, but that Anthropic hopes to show a brand new way of working in Claude. The upgraded interactive connectors let partners embed applications directly into Claude, so users can use tools from vendors such as Adobe while talking to the AI without switching between web pages. Some plug-ins carry preset skills, such as a Salesforce plug-in for sales staff preparing for customer meetings, a NetSuite plug-in for finance staff analyzing data, and a Workday plug-in for human resources handling leave and expenses. Anthropic said its app marketplace now has more than 9,000 connectors and plug-ins, and that Claude's applications are expanding from programmers to non-technical teams such as legal, finance and product management.

Anthropic said its own legal team used Claude to build a legal review tool for Slack that marks content needing changes, shortening review time for marketing materials from three days to 24 hours. Ash Gupta, Director of Financial Planning and Analysis at Advantage Solutions, said his team previously spent about 10 hours per forecasting round on presentation materials, descriptions and verification, and that Claude cut this to less than 30 minutes. HubSpot said account managers can view real-time dashboards in Claude and generate a draft follow-up email within 30 minutes after a call, while Datadog said product managers use Claude to turn ideas into briefs, requirement documents and prototypes faster. Anthropic is not alone in this market, as OpenAI launched the collaborative workspace ChatGPT Space at the end of September and began rolling out ChatGPT Slides to eligible Pro, Business and Enterprise users on October 16.

stories.Headline: Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo moves super AI researcher forecast to 2027
stories.Summary:
On November 11, Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI researcher, shared his team's new prediction on X and said he felt scared, sad and angry. He believes the intelligence explosion will happen in 2027 after all. If METR's judgment holds, the AI-driven R&D acceleration will be about five months earlier than the original deduction in "AI 2027". When AI starts to help humans develop the next generation of AI, even the most radical predictors may underestimate the speed of progress of AI models. In less than three months, AI Futures Project, the prediction team behind "AI 2027", has moved the timeline for the arrival of Super AI Researcher (SAR) to next year.

Previously, Kokotajlo, the most optimistic member of the team, only gave a 50% probability when mentioning that super AI researchers will emerge before 2029. On November 10, AI Futures Project released a new round of forecasts (Q3.5). The signed authors unanimously believe that if there is no significant and active slowdown in cutting-edge AI R&D, super AI researchers are very likely to emerge in 2027. The most important basis that prompted them to change their judgment is a survey of Anthropic conducted by the independent assessment agency METR. METR spent 11 weeks investigating Anthropic, reviewing internal data and interviewing employees, and finally estimated a number.

Since October 2025, the growth rate of the benchmark score of Anthropic's internal models has reached 1.9 times of the previous level. According to this estimate, the one-year increase of Anthropic's models in this set of tests is equivalent to the growth of the past nearly two years. On November 5, METR released this report. In order to see how fast Anthropic's models have improved, METR used an internal indicator called AECI. It combines the scores of multiple tests into a total score, and most tests have clear goals whose results can also be verified.

METR estimates that since October 2025, the growth rate of this total score is about 1.9 times of the previous level, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5 to 2.8 times. Around October 2025, the annual increase in the model's comprehensive score rose from about 15 points to about 29 points. METR recalculated with several different assumptions and found that the score growth rate after October 2025 is about 1.1 to 2.9 times of the previous level. METR examined the changes in training computing power, recruitment, data and algorithms, and believed that the change in the growth rate of training computing power cannot explain this acceleration. However, the specific evidence supporting this judgment has been deleted in the public version of the report.

As for how much contribution AI has made, METR believes that this proportion is also changing over time. When the acceleration just started at the end of 2025, factors other than AI most likely also played a role. But by October 2026, METR estimates that about 80% of the extra speed gain compared to the past may come from AI. METR notes that this "80%" is its subjective estimate, and the report uses "We guess" and clearly points out that this judgment has great uncertainty. One interviewed researcher said that in the past, some ideas would take a day or two just to write code and run experiments.

With the help of AI, he is willing to try more ideas to see which ones work. Other interviewed researchers also mentioned that AI helps write experimental code, monitor experiment operation, and complete some measurements that used to require a lot of extra effort. Some people even give ten ideas to the agent at one time to let it help implement and test them. From writing code to running experiments, AI is already helping to develop the next generation of AI. According to the new estimate of AI Futures Project, this acceleration may come earlier than the original deduction in "AI 2027".

The "AI 2027" released in April 2025 deduced how AI could help develop the next generation of models. According to the setting at that time, the virtual company OpenBrain needed a week and a half to achieve the same amount of algorithm progress without AI, and only one week with AI. But algorithm progress is only part of model progress, and an improvement that comes out of the experiment must be applied to the next round of training to be reflected in the capabilities of the new model. This time, AI Futures Project calculated based on METR's estimate that by early November 2026, the acceleration brought by AI alone may make the overall model progress speed reach 1.7 times of the historical level. In order to see when this speed would appear in the old scenario, the team used the model to reproduce the general trend of "AI 2027".

The results show that the same 1.7x speed will not be reached until around April 2027. If the estimate in early November holds, the time when the model progress speed reaches 1.7 times will be about five months earlier than the old scenario. This result also exceeds the team's expectations less than three months ago. Even according to the most optimistic prediction model at that time, the probability that AI would push the overall model progress speed to 1.7 times or higher of the historical level in November 2026 was less than 4%. METR's report also made AI Futures Project move the timeline for super AI researchers forward.

According to their definition, a super AI researcher must first be able to handle all the programming work of a cutting-edge AI project. In terms of choosing research directions, designing experiments, interpreting results and other matters, it also needs to have the judgment of a top human research team. After the code is written, which idea should be tried next, and when an experiment fails, whether to continue to investigate the cause or change direction, AI has to make these decisions without ready-made answers by itself. In the same report, the time calculated by the three methods differs by more than a year. One method first assumes that AI has pushed the model progress speed to 1.7 times the historical level, then takes into account that AI may take over more R&D work in the future.

According to this model, the median forecast is February 2027, which means that the probability of a super AI researcher emerging before this point in time is about 50%. Another method extrapolates backward according to the speed of the model's progress in the test to estimate when it can have the judgment of a top research team, and the calculated median is July 2027. The third method uses the efficiency improvement reported by Anthropic's own employees to extrapolate, and the result reaches mid-2028. METR stated at the beginning of the report that it believed most of the evidence that is most helpful for judging the core conclusions has been deleted. The report also lists a table that compares item by item what internal materials Anthropic provided to METR and which results were included in the public version.

The benchmark score trend of internal models is made public, but the estimation of algorithm progress and key R&D investment are not disclosed. As for AI's contribution to R&D acceleration, the public version only lists part of the evidence. According to the prior agreement, Anthropic can redact non-public information, and METR can point out which conclusions rely on these materials. Anthropic's reason is that publicizing this confidential information may help other developers accelerate AI R&D. After the redaction, AI Futures Project pointed out that the benchmark score growth rate is about 1.9 times the previous level, which is supported by the public curve. As for the "about 80% of the extra acceleration may come from AI" and the 1.7x speed extrapolated based on it, there is far less public evidence.

To judge whether these two figures are reliable, the outside world relies more on METR's assessment of internal materials. On November 5, METR also released a review of Anthropic's August risk report. Both METR and Anthropic believe that the risk of directly causing a disaster by using the mid-July model to automatically conduct R&D is still relatively low. Both sides also tend to believe that the R&D acceleration at that time had not reached the warning line set by Anthropic. However, METR believes that Anthropic's public report underestimated the magnitude of the acceleration at that time, and the actual acceleration may have already touched the warning line.

Next, we will first see whether AI helping researchers write code and run experiments faster can make the next generation of models delivered earlier. Then we will see whether after this stronger model is put into R&D, it can also shorten the R&D cycle of the next round. If the acceleration can be accumulated generation by generation, Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI) may arrive earlier than expected. The article is from the WeChat official account "AI Era" (ID: AI_era), written by Yuan Yu, and authorized for release by 36Kr. The article states that the views expressed are only those of the author, and that the 36Kr platform only provides information storage space services.
